44588838.article_content:
Foreign YouTube stars secretly paid by UK Government for 'propaganda'
UK Government
YouTube
Media
Scotland
By  Lucy Garcia
Share
The work is being coordinated by Zinc Network Ltd on behalf of the Foreign Office, headed up by David Lammy
(Image: James Manning)
This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
and has been written by our American colleagues.
It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
FOREIGN YouTube stars are being secretly paid by the UK Government to publish "propaganda" videos, it has emerged.
A three-year investigation by Declassified UK
has found that online influencers are made to sign legal contracts banning them from disclosing the Government’s involvement.
"Feedback" on each video is given by Whitehall officials before the influencers are allowed to publish them.
London-based media agency, Zinc Network Ltd – co-founded by a former
Conservative Party
spin doctor – is heading up the work on behalf of the Foreign Office in a deal worth nearly £10 million of public money.
READ MORE:
UK ministers told to increase Scottish Government borrowing limits
Zinc has won lucrative contracts from the UK, US and Australian governments.
Speaking to Declassified, one former employee described Zinc’s work as “state propaganda” and accused it of interference in foreign elections.
Another said the relationship with some online influencers was “extremely exploitative”.
In recent years the company has recruited hundreds of internet celebrities for various clients, particularly in central and eastern Europe.
Influencers are instructed to sign non-disclosure agreements prior to being told about Foreign Office involvement, so anyone watching their videos would have no idea they had been funded and signed-off by
UK Government
officials.
The work has included a campaign to mobilise young voters in the 2023 Slovakian elections. That election was ultimately won by Robert Fico’s left-wing nationalist Smer party, which is seen as being “pro-Russian”.
One former employee said that, by targeting younger voters, Zinc Network’s campaign amounted to “interference in a sovereign country’s internal affairs”.
READ MORE:
Fresh headache for Rachel Reeves as inflation jumps to 18-month high
Zinc Network claims to operate with the “highest standards” of transparency, including a “transparent approach to attribution”.
Rules set out by the UK’s Advertising Standards Agency (ASA) say: “If an influencer is paid in any form… and the brand has shared control over the content, the post must be obviously identifiable as an ad.”
The rules go on to say that “ads mustn’t materially mislead by omitting the identity of the marketer.”
In 2022, Zinc signed a £9,450,000 contract with the Foreign Office, which is due to end in December this year.
Usually, large contracts are published in full on the Government’s website, but in this instance the contract was kept secret.
For almost two years, the Foreign Office tried to prevent it from being released under the Freedom of Information Act, leading to three separate reprimands from the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) who ruled in favour of transparency each time.
A heavily redacted version of the contract was eventually disclosed, although the ICO is now assessing a fresh complaint over the Foreign Office’s refusal to release the document’s full annexes.
The documents show that Zinc was contracted to help counter disinformation in 22 countries across Central, Eastern and Southern Europe, and in the Baltics.
They say: "This project fits within wider 30-year UK Government objectives, to provide balanced, independent voices to more people in the regions.”
In a
response
to a parliamentary question about Zinc last month, the Government admitted it “provides feedback on videos for social media” to “ensure alignment with overarching project objectives, and conflict and gender sensitivity criteria”.
However, the statement added: “Due to the risks posed to our partners and beneficiaries of these projects we do not publish detailed information about them.”
Responding to the investigation, a Foreign Office spokesperson said: “The UK will always champion truth and democratic values. Working with partner governments, we use a range of efforts to resist and rebut disinformation spread by those that wish to target the British people and our allies.
“As part of this important work, we collaborate with commercial organisations, independent media outlets and civil society to combat manipulation and interference in democratic participation.”
Zinc said in a statement: "Zinc Network is proud of our work helping civil society push back against hostile Russian influence, especially given the destruction being wrought on
Ukraine
. We operate within all applicable legislation and our own ethical frameworks around transparency and duty of care, as reviewed by an independent media ethicist."

data.author: lucideng
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI技术的应用及其影响

不同观点：
• 支持观点：
  - [linotype] 认为人们对AI的抱怨是不必要的，可以选择不使用，并指出技术社区对新技术的抵制是不合理的。
  - [DANmode] 建议使用专业级别的设备来获得更好的AI体验，暗示消费级设备的局限性导致了对AI的不满。
  - [rgreekguy] 提到其前公司在AI应用上的积极举措，并认为像Gemini这样的AI工具在某些情况下是有趣且有用的。

• 反对观点：
  - [isntThatSth] 认为并非所有新技术都是有益的，并通过对比智能手机前后的生活，表达了对AI革命的担忧。
  - [blinkbat] 认为大多数人对AI的过度推广感到厌烦，但因为投资者的热捧，普通用户无力改变现状。
  - [sierra1011] 对工作软件中频繁出现的AI提示和通知感到疲惫，且无法关闭这些提示，影响了使用体验。
  - [moomoo11] 对因AI功能而涨价的行为表示不满，认为这对不使用这些功能的用户是不公平的。

• 中立/观望观点：
  - [aspir] 对AI的长期价值持谨慎乐观态度，认为目前只有5%的AI应用会产生实际价值，但需要在大量炒作中筛选出真正有潜力的应用。
  - [Bender] 对AI在产品中的主导地位表示担忧，担心这会导致产品变得臃肿和失去原有的优势，但同时也希望这种担忧是多余的。
  - [jaredcwhite] 预测软件行业可能会因AI的过度推广而经历市场震荡，并认为高端产品可能会逐渐去除AI标签。

• 其他值得注意的观点：
  - [WarOnPrivacy] 提到AI在某些职业中确实有帮助，但同时也指出AI功能的强制植入和难以关闭的问题，反映了用户对AI控制权的担忧。
  - [cadamsdotcom] 认为当前显眼的AI按钮只是一时的潮流，真正的AI应用将是更加 subtle（ subtle这个词在英文中通常指“微妙”或“不易察觉”）。
  - [canistr] 指出类似Bixby的例子，认为对AI功能的过度反应可能忽视了历史上类似的技术问题。

- 争议焦点在于AI功能的强制植入和用户对其控制权的缺失。

主要讨论点：围绕Fyre Festival及其创始人Billy McFarland的商业行为和态度的评价

不同观点：

• **[quantified的观点]**：对Fyre Festival事件持不同的看法，认为尽管该项目最终失败，但其中存在赚钱的机会。quantified用"dumpster fire"（垃圾火灾）来形容Fyre Festival，暗示即便是一个失败的项目，还是有人能够从中获利，并表达了对传统办公室工作的不满或质疑。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：一方认为McFarland没有从失败中学习，依然抱有不切实际的期望；另一方则认为即便是失败的项目，也可能存在商机，反映出对商业失败的不同态度。

• **论据和例子**：cosmicgadget引用了McFarland声称的七位数交易失败作为其不接受现实的证据。quantified则隐含地指出失败项目中也可能存在未开发的经济潜力，虽然没有提供具体例子。

• **讨论关系**：两种观点形成对比，一个侧重于McFarland个人的态度和行为，另一个则关注于商业机会的存在，即便是在失败的项目中。

data.title: Near-cryogenic direct air capture using adsorbents
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了一种近低温直接空气捕碳（DAC）方法，利用物理吸附剂在160–220 K温度范围内实现高效的二氧化碳捕集。研究结合液化天然气（LNG）再气化过程中产生的冷能，选取Zeolite 13X和CALF-20作为吸附材料，实验表明其二氧化碳吸附量达4.5–5.5 mmol/g，且具有低脱附焓和高稳定性。该方法可将捕碳成本降至68.2美元/吨，并借助全球LNG再气化资源，预计到2050年可每年捕集1.03–1.42亿吨二氧化碳。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效利用冷的液化天然气（LNG）中的能量，以及该过程是否已经通过现有技术实现。

不同观点：
• 观点一：nullc认为，目前已经有方法通过利用传统的天然气发电机运行，将废热用于预热LNG，然后利用产生的高压输出驱动涡轮机，从而捕捉LNG中的能量。这种方法的效率足够高，以至于有人提议将液化空气与天然气调峰机组结合使用，作为一种具有竞争力的能量储存技术。这种方法利用了通常无法有效利用的低品位废热，并且在需要放电时，天然气调峰机组正好运行，从而提高了整体效率。

• 观点二：有人可能认为，LNG冷能的利用过程效率较低，特别是液化空气的往返效率较差，可能导致整体能量利用效率不高。这种观点质疑通过天然气废热来补偿低效液化空气过程的可行性。

补充讨论：
• nullc提到，液化空气的储存技术与天然气调峰机组结合，可以在需要时有效放电，并且这种方法可以利用传统热沉无法有效利用的低品位废热。

• 争议的焦点在于LNG冷能利用过程的整体效率以及该技术在实际应用中的经济性和可行性。一方认为通过结合天然气调峰机组可以提高效率，另一方则可能质疑该过程的往返效率和实际应用价值。

• 论据包括利用废热提高效率的具体技术路径（如预热LNG并驱动涡轮机）以及液化空气作为能量储存技术的潜力。这些论据为支持各自观点提供了技术细节和实际应用案例。

Abstract
Direct air capture (DAC) of CO
2
is a key component in the portfolio of negative emissions technologies for mitigating global warming. However, even with the most potent amine sorbents, large-scale DAC deployment remains limited by high energy and capital costs. Recently, adsorbents relying on weak interactions with CO
2
have emerged as a potential alternative, thanks to their rapid adsorption kinetics and superior long-term stability, particularly under sub-ambient conditions (∼253 K). Despite these advantages, their use is hindered by the need for a water-removal process, location-specific constraints, and insufficient working capacity even in cold climates. In this study, we hypothesized that further reducing the adsorption temperature to a near-cryogenic range (160–220 K) could enable cost-effective DAC by utilizing the full potential of physisorbents. We primarily consider integrating DAC with a relatively untapped source of cold energy—liquified natural gas (LNG) regasification—to perform near-cryogenic DAC. From large-scale molecular simulations, Zeolite 13X and CALF-20 were identified as promising candidates. These materials were subsequently examined through experiments, including breakthrough analyses at 195 K. Their high CO
2
sorption capacity (4.5–5.5 mmol g
−1
), combined with a low desorption enthalpy and robust long-term stability, led to a threefold reduction in the levelized cost of capture (down to 68.2 USD per tonne CO
2
). Estimates of the global LNG regasification resource suggest that LNG–DAC coupling could potentially enable the capture of 103–142 megatonnes of CO
2
annually as of 2050.

data.title: Where's Firefox going next?
data.author: ReadCarlBarks
data.article_summary: Mozilla正在邀请Firefox用户参与互动，以帮助塑造浏览器的未来。过去，诸如标签组、垂直标签、新标签壁纸等功能都是根据用户反馈开发的。现在，他们计划通过一系列快速调查，进一步了解用户的需求和想法。Mozilla还准备举办一场社区AMA（Ask Me Anything）活动，邀请用户提出问题并讨论新功能和浏览器发展方向。用户可以提出他们一直想问Firefox团队的问题，并建议AMA中应涵盖的主题。一些用户反馈提到希望增强多任务处理功能、增加界面灵活性，并对AI功能缺乏对西里尔字母的支持表示关注。Mozilla感谢用户的参与和支持，并希望继续共同改进Firefox。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Mozilla及其产品（特别是Firefox）的多种批评和建议，涉及营销方式、产品功能、技术决策、隐私保护以及公司方向等问题。

不同观点：
• **营销和社区互动方式**：
  - [idle_zealot] 认为Mozilla的营销和社区互动方式显得幼稚和表面化，像对待幼儿园孩子一样对待用户，尤其是使用动物表情符号来代表浏览风格让他感到不满。
  - 该用户强调，自己并不反对幽默或有趣的宣传，但Mozilla的方式显得人工化和过度甜腻。

• **财务与管理问题**：
  - [JumpCrisscross] 关注Mozilla的捐款是否与CEO的薪酬相近，引用了2023年和2022年的财务报告数据，质疑其资金使用情况。
  - [promiseofbeans] 对比了Thunderbird和Mozilla的捐款收入，指出如果Mozilla能像Thunderbird那样明确资金用途，可能会获得更多支持。

• **产品功能与用户体验**：
  - [aucisson_masque] 指出Firefox在移动端和桌面端存在界面设计问题，如过多的历史记录选项、地址栏按钮过多等，认为Mozilla知道用户需求但未能有效实现。
  - [captainepoch] 建议Mozilla停止浪费资源在无关紧要的项目上，应专注于社区反馈，雇佣工程师提升浏览器性能。
  - [gfdjghd] 也提到Firefox Android版地址栏按钮过多，界面不友好，并建议增加自定义选项。
  - [jjordan] 怀念已移除的“智能书签”功能，并提到有第三方插件部分复现了该功能，但仍希望官方恢复支持。

• **隐私与竞争问题**：
  - [bigiain] 认为Mozilla被广告和监控公司控制，无法真正专注于用户隐私保护，这是比其他问题更重要的核心问题。
  - [tsoukas] 推测Google通过资金支持影响Mozilla的决策，使其保持低市场份额并避免对Google构成实质竞争。

• **技术支持与扩展功能**：
  - [mijoharas] 希望Firefox支持WebUSB功能，并改进扩展API对favicon的处理，以提高使用体验。
  - [v5v3] 建议Firefox在隐私模式下支持容器功能，并增加类似Safari的锁定模式，以增强安全性。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户对Mozilla的发展方向感到失望，认为其浪费资源且未能满足用户需求，导致市场份额下降。
• 部分用户提到具体的技术功能和界面改进建议，显示出对浏览器细节的高度关注。
• 隐私和广告问题成为用户关注的焦点，尤其是对Mozilla是否能真正独立于大型商业利益集团表示担忧。

data.title: Hierarchical Modeling (H-Nets)
data.author: lukebechtel
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种新的AI架构——层次网络（H-Nets），旨在解决当前模型在处理原始数据时缺乏层次结构的局限性。传统模型对所有输入一视同仁，处理高分辨率原始数据时需要预处理，且对输入的小变动敏感，计算资源浪费较多。H-Nets通过动态分块机制，将数据分段为有意义的概念，包含编码器、主网络和 decoder三个部分。实验显示，H-Nets在语言建模上优于最先进的Transformer模型，尤其在无自然分词边界的领域表现更佳；它还能通过更深层次提高性能，对输入扰动更具鲁棒性。H-Nets有助于多模态数据融合、长上下文推理及提高训练和推理效率，代表了AI架构的重要进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：H-Net语言模型的潜在优势及其与现有模型的对比

不同观点：
• **H-Net的优势与未来发展**：
  - lukebechtel认为H-Net在数据扩展性、处理无自然分词边界的领域（如中文、代码、DNA）以及对输入扰动的鲁棒性方面表现优异，展示了未来发展潜力。
  - modeless支持这一观点，认为通过增加层次结构可以更有效地处理长序列和高层次结构，并提到Byte Latent Transformers的延伸想法与H-Net类似。

• **H-Net的独特性与相关技术对比**：
  - cs702对H-Net的层次组合和路由方面与heinsen_routing技术进行了比较，认为两者虽不同，但在基于相似性的路由上有所关联。
  - notreallymetho提到H-Net让他想起自己曾做过的相关工作，但未详细说明。

• **对语言层次结构的质疑与扩展**：
  - macawfish不完全认同“语言本质上是层次化的”这一观点，认为不应只依赖单一层次结构，建议学习多个层次并学会在它们之间调制。

• **对模型处理输入方式的疑问**：
  - vannevar质疑H-Net是否真的与现有模型在处理输入上有本质区别，认为许多模型在训练时都会推断层次结构。

• **H-Net在其他领域的应用潜力**：
  - aeon_ai认为H-Net可能对记忆形成、巩固和管理有重要意义。
  - gdiamos询问H-Net如何处理图像。

• **H-Net是否会取代Transformers**：
  - cubefox提出H-Net是否会像Mamba一样未能取代Transformers的问题。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到H-Net在层次结构和处理不同类型数据（如语言、图像、DNA）方面的潜在优势，但也存在对其独特性和实际应用效果的质疑和讨论。
- 一些评论者分享了相关技术链接和个人经验，试图进一步探讨H-Net与现有技术的异同。

44574990.article_content:
Jul 11, 2025
Â·
Research
Hierarchical modeling
Hierarchical modeling
Albert Gu
Brandon Wang
The best AI architectures in use today treat all inputs equally. They process each input with the same amount of compute, without explicitly grouping related inputs into higher level concepts. While these architectures have achieved impressive results across domains, this lack of hierarchy has some fundamental limitations.
Models have difficulty learning from high resolution, raw data, requiring inputs to be pre-processed into meaningful tokens for strong performance.
The use of hand-crafted pre-processing steps (e.g. tokenization) can cause models to fail unexpectedly with small perturbations in the input data.
Models waste compute on tokens that are easy to predict and not informative.
More importantly, information is fundamentally hierarchical. In language, ideas are chunked in characters, words, sentences, and paragraphs; in images, pixels are chunked in edges, shapes, and objects; in audio, raw waveforms are grouped into phonemes, sentences, and conversation turns. As humans, we consume raw information and group it in meaningful ways that allow us to reason and make connections at different levels of abstraction, from low level units to the high level ideas. This is core to intelligence. We believe hierarchical models will address several of the fundamental limitations and shortcomings of todayâs architectures.
Weâre excited to announce our latest research collaboration on
hierarchical networks (H-Nets)
, a new architecture that natively models hierarchy from raw data. The core of the H-Net architecture is a dynamic chunking mechanism that learns to segment and compress raw data into meaningful concepts for modeling. It has three components: an encoder network, the main network, and a decoder network. The core of the encoder network is a routing module, which uses a similarity score to predict groups of meaningful chunks that should be grouped together and compressed for the main network. The main network can be any sequence to sequence model, and is responsible for next token prediction over these higher level chunks. Finally, the decoder network learns to decode chunks back into raw data, with a smoothing module for stabilizing learning.
H-Net demonstrates three important results on language modeling:
H-Nets scale better with data than state-of-the-art Transformers with BPE tokenization, while learning directly from raw bytes. This improved scaling is even more pronounced on domains without natural tokenization boundaries, like Chinese, code, and DNA.
H-Nets can be stacked together to learn from deeper hierarchies, which further improves performance.
H-Nets are significantly more robust to small perturbations in input data like casing, showing an avenue for creating models that are more robust and aligned with human reasoning.
Our investment in this research is part of our larger push to build the next-generation of AI models that are multimodal, highly efficient, and reason and improve over long horizons. State space models represented our first research advancement, enabling stateful models that can compress information over long contexts. We believe H-Nets, and hierarchical modeling, are the key next step to addressing fundamental challenges in AI:
Multimodal understanding and generation:
A key challenge in multimodal modeling is fusing multiple streams of data. This is a difficult today, since different modalities are tokenized at different rates. For example, language is tokenized into subwords, while audio is tokenized as raw waveforms or downsampled codecs. This makes them difficult to model jointly. Hierarchical models like H-Net provide a promising path to fuse these multimodal streams at a higher abstraction level, enabling better transfer, reasoning, and understanding across modalities.
Long-context reasoning:
H-Nets unlock long context reasoning by chunking information into semantically meaningful units at higher levels of abstraction. This compression makes it easier for models to understand and reason across large inputs, particularly with deeper and deeper hierarchies. Hierarchical architectures will enable models that understand their environment from raw data and reason at appropriate levels of abstraction over long horizons.
Efficient training and inference:
Todayâs architectures use the same amount of compute for every token, even though some tokens are less informative and easier to predict than others. Inference time optimizations, like speculative decoding, exploit this property to speed up computation on easier to predict tokens. With H-Nets, this is built directly into the architecture, by handling tokens that are easier to predict with lightweight encoder and decoder modules.
For more, read our full preprint on
arXiv
. Weâve also released checkpoints for H-Net 2-stage XL, H-Net 1-stage XL, and H-Net 1-stage L on
HuggingFace
.

data.title: Xbox Hacks: The A20 (2021)
data.author: mattweinberg
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Xbox的一个硬件漏洞，即A20地址线问题，该问题源于早期Intel 8088 CPU的设计限制。最初，8088 CPU只有20条地址线，最大可寻址1MB内存。由于16位寄存器需要通过位移转换来映射到20位物理地址，当请求超出20位地址限制的内存时，地址会出现“回绕”现象，即超出部分会被截断并从低地址重新开始。

IBM在推出PC/AT时，为兼容旧系统，在主板上增加了一个A20门控信号，以模拟旧CPU的地址回绕特性。这一设计后来被沿用至包括Pentium III在内的后续CPU中。在Xbox中，利用这一漏洞可以通过控制A20地址线，使系统绕过安全启动流程，直接从闪存启动，从而带来安全风险。这一发现归功于Xbox Linux项目和研究者Michael Steil。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：A20地址环绕（A20 gate）相关的历史、技术细节及其在不同系统中的应用和影响

不同观点：
• **A20地址环绕的历史和应用**：userbinator分享了一系列文章链接，探讨了依赖A20地址环绕的软件及其历史背景，指出该功能在早期的系统和软件（如WordStar等）中具有实际作用。

• **A20地址环绕的硬件实现**：messe补充了关于A20 gate如何通过键盘控制器寄存器实现切换的技术细节，认为这种设计选择可能是为了最小化硬件重新设计的工作量，是一种在嵌入式系统开发中常见的做法。

• **A20相关问题的持续存在**：mjg59提到A20相关的bug直到2009年依然存在，并分享了一个个人经历和可视化解释，展示了该问题如何在实际中出现。

• **A20在现代系统中的应用**：junon指出，构建操作系统时，仍然需要在bootloader中处理A20地址环绕问题，表明这一历史遗留问题在现代系统中仍有影响。

• **Xbox中的A20问题**：pwdisswordfishz对Xbox中启用A20功能的目的表示困惑，并指出这实际上是经过硬件修改实现的，而非Xbox原生需求。

• **推荐相关视频**：msk-lywenn推荐了一个关于解构Xbox的有趣演讲视频，暗示对了解A20及相关技术有帮助。

补充讨论：
• **对游戏平台的讨论**：heraldgeezer表达了对在Xbox上运行PS2游戏的想象，同时赞扬了Halo 2游戏的独特性，将讨论引向了游戏体验和平台对比的方向。

争议焦点：
• **Xbox中启用A20功能的必要性**：pwdisswordfishz对Xbox为何启用A20功能表示不解，并通过提供链接表明这是硬件修改的结果，而非Xbox本身设计所需。这与其他人讨论的A20在其他系统中的必要性形成对比。

总结：
讨论围绕A20地址环绕的历史、技术实现及其在不同系统中的应用展开，参与者分享了相关的技术细节、实际案例和个人见解，并延伸到了具体游戏平台的讨论。争议点集中在Xbox中A20功能的实际需求和实现方式上。

In November of this year (2021) we will hit 20 years since the release of the original Xbox. This console was full of vulnerabilities (or misconfiguration) from the software to the hardware and with such a low price point two decades ago for a computer - it was highly popular. For this post we are going to go into a lot of details regarding one mistake Microsoft made which was the A20.

Intel 8088 (1978) -
Credit - CPUShack
So lets start with some history with some real old CPUs starting with the Intel 8088, which thanks to the
CPUShack
reminds us it started production in 1978 and lasted till 1998. This CPU had 20 physical address lines labeled A0 through A19 and each line represents a simple binary (0/1) so you can store 2
20
bytes or 1 MB of information.
A rough drawing of address lines to RAM (A0-A19) on an Intel 8088
However, the 4 registers (code segment - CS, data segment - DS, stack segment - SS and extra segment - ES) only had 16 bits. So some form of translation needed to occur to map 16 bit registers to physical address space of 20 bits. This is where the small calculation came to be:
segment (shifted 4 bits) + offset = address
.
Internal Address -> Physical Address
So I wrote up a quick example to show how addresses translate into a physical address. Since we are shifting 4 bits, we can easily do 2
4
(2*2*2*2) and get 16 decimal or 0
x
10 hex to multiple the address by.
The thing about this notation is you can represent physical addresses with so many possible internal address + offset pairs. So knowing the early Intel 8088 only had 1MB what would happen if you asked for the memory at segment -
0
x
F800
, with offset

8000
. I'll save the long math and just say you'll get the physical address at

which is over the limit of a 20 bit address. The last real value would be at location
0
x
000FFFFF
, so the older generation CPUs just dropped any bit above the 20
th
.
So taking
0
x
00100000
would require a 21
st
bit, which doesn't exist on the Intel 8088 thus it gets dropped which ends up changing the location to
0
x
00000000
. This is known commonly as a "wraparound" because the location wraps back around to the beginning (or end) depending on how you are reading the memory.
Images from CPUShack - Intel 8028x
So the story gets interesting when you look at the history as a whole. For example, take the
Intel 80286
which still rocked a 16 bit processor, but had 16 MB instead of 1 MB memory. This meant it had 24 address lines instead of 20, which wouldn't mean much except for when IBM started building the
PC/AT
(1984). The machine had additional memory, but broke compatibility with previous solutions that depended on the implicit "wraparound" that occurred when requesting memory outside the limitation of the address lines.
If you had trouble visualizing that, the image above should show the 20 address lines on the 8088, as well as laying the additional 4 address lines that the 80286 had above. So you can see it was not possible to represent a 21 digit binary number with only 20 lines.
So IBM probably panicked at this point - they can't swap microprocessors at this point, so they tweaked the motherboard by placing a gate on the A20 address line. So depending on signal given to the gate it could be thrown to 0, thus effectively mimicking the behavior of the older Intel 8088 if warranted. This could effectively swap the system between legacy behavior or the new.
I've attempted to build an over simplified drawing to depict this, since the image above incorrectly assumes the gate exists at the CPU level, when in 1984 it did not.
Another rough drawing of the IBM PC/AT
So I think you can see where this is going now. This feature which IBM started eventually moved into the CPU and started being included in a few of the later CPUs including the Pentium series.
The lucky original Xbox was packing a 32 bit 733 MHz Intel Pentium III processor, which indeed had this A20# Gate. So knowing the Xbox boots up (after some initialization) at
0
x
FFFFFFF0
, if we ground the A20 line - the Xbox will instead boot at
0
x
FFEFFFF0
. So once again another quick and dirty drawing to explain how this will affect the process.
A partial memory map of the original Xbox
So you can see a normal Xbox boots into the secure state of the ROM. This is the portion that sets up enough critical information to verify and run the 2nd boot-loader (2BL) which then proceeds to also verify and prepare the kernel. However, grounding the A20 line proceeds to boot the Xbox directly into flash.
This is not good for Microsoft from a security perspective. The system can now boot from flash with whatever was cleverly placed there. An added bonus that booting with the A20 line grounded keeps
44589384.article_summary:
本文讨论了Xbox的一个硬件漏洞，即A20地址线问题，该问题源于早期Intel 8088 CPU的设计限制。最初，8088 CPU只有20条地址线，最大可寻址1MB内存。由于16位寄存器需要通过位移转换来映射到20位物理地址，当请求超出20位地址限制的内存时，地址会出现“回绕”现象，即超出部分会被截断并从低地址重新开始。

IBM在推出PC/AT时，为兼容旧系统，在主板上增加了一个A20门控信号，以模拟旧CPU的地址回绕特性。这一设计后来被沿用至包括Pentium III在内的后续CPU中。在Xbox中，利用这一漏洞可以通过控制A20地址线，使系统绕过安全启动流程，直接从闪存启动，从而带来安全风险。这一发现归功于Xbox Linux项目和研究者Michael Steil。

data.title: Show HN: Linux CLI tool to provide mutex locks for long running bash ops
data.author: bigattichouse
data.article_summary:
WaitLock 是一个用于 UNIX/POSIX 系统的命令行工具，提供互斥锁和信号量功能，确保长时运行的 shell 脚本在多进程环境下的资源同步访问。其主要功能包括：

1. **互斥模式**：单个锁持有者。
2. **信号量模式**：允许多个并发锁持有者。
3. **自动清理**：进程终止时自动释放锁。
4. **CPU感知锁定**：根据 CPU 数量调整锁。
5. **锁检查**：列出和检查活跃锁。
6. **多种输出格式**：人类可读、CSV 和空字符分隔。
7. **命令执行**：在持有锁时运行命令。
8. **UNIX集成**：支持环境变量、stdin、syslog。

**安装**：
```bash
sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf
git clone https://github.com/user/waitlock.git
cd waitlock
./configure
make
sudo make install
```

**基本使用**：
```bash
# 获取互斥锁
waitlock myapp &
# 执行命令并持有锁
waitlock database_backup --exec "/usr/local/bin/backup.sh --daily"
# 列出活跃锁
waitlock --list
```

WaitLock 支持超时、CPU感知、锁监控等多种高级功能，适用于需要严格进程同步的脚本任务。

WaitLock
WaitLock
is a portable UNIX/POSIX command-line tool that provides mutex and semaphore functionality for shell scripts. It enables synchronized access to resources across multiple processes with automatic cleanup when processes die.
Features
Mutex Mode
: Single lock holder (default)
Semaphore Mode
: Multiple concurrent lock holders
Automatic Cleanup
: Locks released when process dies
CPU-aware Locking
: Can scale locks to CPU count
Lock Inspection
: List and check active locks
Multiple Output Formats
: Human, CSV, and null-separated
Command Execution
: Run commands while holding locks
UNIX Integration
: Environment variables, stdin, syslog
Portable C Implementation
: Runs on any POSIX system
Quick Start
#
Install dependencies (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf
#
Build and install
./configure
make
sudo make install
#
Basic usage - acquire exclusive lock
waitlock myapp
&
#
... do exclusive work ...
kill
$!
#
Execute command with lock
waitlock database_backup --exec
"
/usr/local/bin/backup.sh --daily
"
#
List active locks
waitlock --list
Table of Contents
Installation
Usage
Examples
Command Reference
Environment Variables
Exit Codes
Advanced Usage
Contributing
License
Installation
From Source
Prerequisites
C compiler (gcc, clang, or compatible)
GNU Make
autoconf (for building from git)
Build Instructions
#
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/user/waitlock.git
cd
waitlock
#
Generate configure script (if building from git)
autoreconf -fi
#
Configure and build
./configure
make
#
Run tests
make check
#
Install system-wide
sudo make install
#
Or install to custom prefix
./configure --prefix=/usr/local
make install
Build Options
#
Debug build
./configure CFLAGS=
"
-g -O0 -DDEBUG
"
#
Release build with optimizations
./configure CFLAGS=
"
-O2 -DNDEBUG
"
#
Cross-compilation example
./configure --host=arm-linux-gnueabihf
Package Installation
#
Ubuntu/Debian (when available)
sudo apt-get install waitlock
#
CentOS/RHEL (when available)
sudo yum install waitlock
#
macOS with Homebrew (when available)
brew install waitlock
Usage
Basic Syntax
waitlock [options]
<
descriptor
>
waitlock --list [--format
=<
fmt
>
] [--all
|
--stale-only]
waitlock --check
<
descriptor
>
echo
<
descriptor
>
|
waitlock [options]
Simple Examples
#
Acquire mutex lock
waitlock myapp
&
JOB_PID=
$!
#
... do exclusive work ...
kill
$JOB_PID
#
Check if lock is available
if
waitlock --check myapp
;
then
echo
"
Lock is available
"
else
echo
"
Lock is held by another process
"
fi
#
Execute command while holding lock
waitlock backup_job --exec rsync -av /source /destination
#
Use with timeout
waitlock --timeout 30 critical_resource
||
echo
"
Timeout!
"
Examples
1. Basic Mutex (Exclusive Access)
#!
/bin/bash
#
Ensure only one backup process runs at a time
waitlock database_backup
||
{
echo
"
Another backup is already running
"
exit
1
}
#
Perform backup
mysqldump --all-databases
>
backup.sql
gzip backup.sql
#
Lock automatically released when script exits
2. Semaphore (Multiple Concurrent Access)
#!
/bin/bash
#
Allow up to 4 concurrent download processes
waitlock --allowMultiple 4 download_pool
||
{
echo
"
Too many downloads already running
"
exit
1
}
#
Perform download
wget
"
https://example.com/file.tar.gz
"
#
Lock automatically released when script exits
3. CPU-Based Semaphore
#!
/bin/bash
#
Use one lock per CPU core, reserving 2 cores for system
waitlock --onePerCPU --excludeCPUs 2 cpu_intensive_task
||
{
echo
"
All CPU slots are busy
"
exit
1
}
#
Run CPU-intensive task
./compute_job.sh
4. Command Execution Mode
#!
/bin/bash
#
Execute command while holding lock (recommended approach)
waitlock database_backup --exec bash -c
"
mysqldump --all-databases > backup.sql
gzip backup.sql
echo 'Backup completed'
"
5. Lock Monitoring and Management
#!
/bin/bash
#
Monitor active locks
#
List all locks in human-readable format
waitlock --list
#
List in CSV format for parsing
waitlock --list --format csv
#
Show only stale locks
waitlock --list --stale-only
#
Count active locks
waitlock --list --format csv
|
tail -n +2
|
wc -l
6. Pipeline and Batch Processing
#!
/bin/bash
#
Process files with controlled parallelism
find /data -name
"
*.csv
"
|
while
read
file
;
do
basen

44561300.article_content:
Where the Horses Swim
Reporting
Photo Essay
Jul 8
Written By
Ana Sotelo
On Barbados’ Pebbles Beach, racehorses train in the ocean.
JULY 8, 2025
Every morning at dawn, on the shores of Pebbles Beach, Barbados, a captivating ritual takes place. Guided by their grooms, racehorses wade into the sea to train and stretch their muscles in the cool saltwater. Most of the horses come from the nearby Garrison Savannah, one of the oldest horse racetracks in the Americas and the Caribbean; others are from local stables or from smaller farms across the island.
At the beach, the routine starts with a practice known as lunging, in which the horse travels in a circle around the groom’s rein handle in the shallows. In deeper water, the groom will push his body against the horse to train its resistance. Afterward, the groom guides the horse into open waters, hanging from its neck, as the horse swims out, sometimes for miles. Tourists and locals alike gather at the beach as the sun rises to catch a glimpse of the daily exercises. When the groom and the horse get back to shore, the groom scrubs down the horse before both head back to the stables and get ready to start training at the track.
Horse racing came to Barbados in 1845: Members of the British Army, who were stationed at Garrison Savannah, would race their horses against those of the sugar-cane plantation owners. Horse racing has since become an important part of Bajan culture and islanders take great pride in the tradition. Races are organized by the Barbados Turf Club and take place at the historic Garrison Savannah racetrack every Saturday. Big races, like the Boxing Day Race, sell out quickly, and for a couple of hours, the island’s attention shifts from its relaxing beaches to the excitement of the racetrack.
A man and horse glide beneath the Caribbean Sea. The daily ritual helps the horses prepare for races and recover from the strain of training.
At dawn, sometimes as early as 4 a.m., grooms and their horses take over Pebbles Beach. Curious tourists and locals gather on the beach to watch.
Hayden, who has been a horse groom since he was 16, scrubs down Dream Lake after a swim. He feeds, cleans and looks after two horses between training and races.
A groom guides a horse into the sea. To help the horse stretch and warm up, the groom pushes his body against the horse's chest.
Jammin, one the oldest grooms on the island, returns from swimming in the open waters with his horse.
Daffy, a horse groom, is one of the first to arrive at Pebbles Beach. The beach’s proximity to the racetrack and the lack of strong currents make it ideal for the horses’ water exercises.
Back at the stables, Hayden rinses Dream Lake with fresh water. He will then take the horse to the racetrack where a trainer will prepare it for the next race.
Spectators begin to fill the Garrison Savannah racetrack ahead of the annual Boxing Day Race — one of the island’s most popular events. Most people arrive at the racetrack several hours before it starts to secure their spot and place bets.
The Boxing Day Race includes eight separate races. The viewing area is packed, and there's an atmosphere of celebration and anticipation.
On his way back from the beach, Daffy passes the Barbados Turf Club, the organization that regulates horse racing in Barbados.
Two children celebrate Bajan jockey Jeremiah Worrell and his horse Gunsmoke before the fourth race of the Boxing Day Race.

originally published
in
Gatopardo.

data.title: 1990 Networking: LAN Manager 2.0
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
微软于1990年发布了LAN Manager (LM) 2.0，这是其网络产品系列中的一部分，最早可追溯到1984年的MS-NET，最终演变为Windows NT文件共享。LM 1.0于1988年作为OEM产品发布，微软与3Com合作并共同发布了网络驱动程序的NDIS规范。然而，1990年微软决定直接销售盒装版LM 2.0，绕过OEM，导致双方关系恶化。

关于LM 2.0的发布时间存在争议。有证据显示1990年6月底微软完成了“最终”版本，但缺乏明确的官方发布声明。一份1990年8月的关于OS/2 1.21的新闻稿提到LM 2.0服务器需要OS/2 1.21，且LM 2.0未与OS/2捆绑销售。而InfoWorld杂志指出，3Com于1990年9月底发布了基于LM 2.0的3+Open，并称LM 2.0于1990年8月由微软发布。

识别LM 2.0的具体版本较为复杂，因其不支持NET VER命令。文件LANMAN.CSD显示，1990年6月的版本为CSD 0（初始版本），而1990年11月的版本为CSD 2（LM 2.0b）。KB文章进一步确认CSD 1为LM 2.00a，CSD 2为LM 2.00b。

44589415.article_content:
In 1990, Microsoft released LAN Manager (LM) 2.0, a member of a long line of Microsoft’s networking products that started with MS-NET circa 1984 and eventually morphed into Windows NT file sharing.
Microsoft LAN Manager 2.0 admin interface
LAN Manager 1.0 was released in 1988 as an OEM-only product, with the largest OEM being 3Com and their
3+Open
. Microsoft collaborated with 3Com
1
and the two companies jointly published the NDIS specification for network drivers. However, the relationship soured in 1990 after Microsoft decided to sell shrink-wrapped LAN Manager directly and bypass OEMs.
LAN Manager 2.0 (2.0b) installation disks
The OS/2 Museum owns a boxed copy of Microsoft LAN Manager 2.0 from circa December 1990, but recently a pirated copy of LM 2.0 from June 1990 came to light, found right next to MS OS/2 1.21 disks. That brought an obvious and simple question: When was LAN Manager 2.0 released? The answer, is unfortunately far from simple.
Besides the warez archive, there is
physical evidence
that Microsoft built
something
at the end of June 1990 and that it was the “final” release of LAN Manager 2.0. Normally a press release would answer a lot of questions, but one for LM 2.0 has remained rather elusive so far. The closest thing we have is
this press release about OS/2 1.21
from August 1990. But it happens to be highly relevant.
The press release clearly explains that LAN Manager 2.0 server requires OS/2 1.21. But that was an OEM product, and end users could not buy OS/2 1.21 from Microsoft directly. LAN Manager 2.0 was also not bundled with OS/2, unlike LM 2.1 and later releases (which came with
MS OS/2 1.3
included). Even if Microsoft did have boxed LM 2.0 copies ready to go in early July 1990, they could not easily sell them because OS/2 1.21 was not available. The OEM fastest to ship OS/2 1.21 was likely Compaq, and they did so perhaps in late August or in September 1990.
Also in the press release is the following statement: “LAN Manager version 2.0 will ship during the month of August.” It is unfortunately unclear whether that was LM 2.0 directly from Microsoft or through OEMs. According to InfoWorld
2
, 3Com released 3+Open based on LAN Manager 2.0 at the end of September 1990. A February 1991 InfoWorld review
3
of networking products says that “[v]ersion 2.0 of LAN Manager, released in August 1990, is a Microsoft shrink-wrapped product”. Perhaps Microsoft did ship LAN Manager 2.0 in August 1990 then, but so far there’s no truly solid evidence one way or another.
A
supplemental readme file
included with MS-DOS 5.0 states: “If the files are dated before June 1990, you have [LAN Manager] version 1.x. Files dated after June 1990 are typically version 2.0.” (The second sentence was probably meant to read “Files dated June 1990 or later”.) That suggests the LM 2.0 files dated June 1990 did make it to end users, whether through OEMs or Microsoft directly.
LAN Manager 2.0 Updates
Another, somewhat indirect source of information is Microsoft KB articles. Many of those were deleted from the KB database long ago, but can be found on old CD-ROMs. The KB articles provide valuable information about the (numerous!) updates to LM 2.0.
KB article
Q66122
talks of a golden release of “LAN Manager version 2.00 packaged product”, and a CSD1. CSD means Corrective Service Diskette, and CSD1 is IBM-speak for patch level 1.
Identifying the specific LM 2.0 version is not particularly easy. LAN Manager 2.0 unfortunately does not support the
NET VER
command at all (that came in LM 2.1). The full-screen NET interface only shows “Version 2.0” regardless of the CSD level. Timestamps can help, but OEM releases of LAN Manager are likely to have modified timestamps not matching the Microsoft originals.
But LAN Manager 2.0 disks come with files called LANMAN.CSD which ought to identify the precise version. Rather surprisingly, this mechanism does not appear to have been documented by Microsoft.
The June 1990 version of OS/2 Workstation 3 disk has a LANMAN.CSD file dated June 28, 1990 that looks like this:
MS LANMAN2.0 FOR OS/2
CURRENT CSD LEVEL = 0
PRIOR CSD LEVEL = 0
CSD level zero implies the first release. The Microsoft-branded LAN Manager disks from late 1990 (which just say “Version 2.0” on the Setup disk without anything closer) have a LANMAN.CSD file dated November 19, 1990 with the following contents:
MS LAN Manager
Version 2.0 Component ID 000111990
Current CSD Level: LM000002
Last CSD Level: LM000001
Note that the format of the file changed. And the CSD file suggests that it’s not the first but rather second update. This is where KB article
Q69738
comes to the rescue, showing the following list:
CSD 1 is LAN Manager 2.00a.
CSD 2 is LAN Manager 2.00b.
CSD 3 is LAN Manager 2.00b for MP.

44589415.article_summary:
微软于1990年发布了LAN Manager (LM) 2.0，这是其网络产品系列中的一部分，最早可追溯到1984年的MS-NET，最终演变为Windows NT文件共享。LM 1.0于1988年作为OEM产品发布，微软与3Com合作并共同发布了网络驱动程序的NDIS规范。然而，1990年微软决定直接销售盒装版LM 2.0，绕过OEM，导致双方关系恶化。

关于LM 2.0的发布时间存在争议。有证据显示1990年6月底微软完成了“最终”版本，但缺乏明确的官方发布声明。一份1990年8月的关于OS/2 1.21的新闻稿提到LM 2.0服务器需要OS/2 1.21，且LM 2.0未与OS/2捆绑销售。而InfoWorld杂志指出，3Com于1990年9月底发布了基于LM 2.0的3+Open，并称LM 2.0于1990年8月由微软发布。

识别LM 2.0的具体版本较为复杂，因其不支持NET VER命令。文件LANMAN.CSD显示，1990年6月的版本为CSD 0（初始版本），而1990年11月的版本为CSD 2（LM 2.0b）。KB文章进一步确认CSD 1为LM 2.00a，CSD 2为LM 2.00b。

data.title: NIST ion clock sets new record for most accurate clock
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）的研究人员开发出世界上最精确的原子钟，能够将时间测量到小数点后19位。这种“量子逻辑钟”基于一个被捕获的铝离子，经过20年的持续改进，其精度比之前的记录高出41%，稳定性也提高了2.6倍。该钟通过量子计算技术，将一个带电的铝离子与一个镁离子配对，以实现精确的时间测量。铝离子的“ ticking”频率非常稳定，受环境条件影响较小。为了解决铝离子难以直接用激光探测和冷却的问题，研究团队利用镁离子辅助冷却和读出时间，形成“量子逻辑光谱”技术。团队还改进了离子阱设计，减少了影响精度的微小运动。这一成果有助于重新定义“秒”，并推动科学和技术进步。研究结果发表在《物理评论快报》上。

NEWS
NIST Ion Clock Sets New Record for Most Accurate Clock in the World
July 14, 2025
Share
Facebook
Linkedin
X.com
Email
NIST researchers have made the most accurate atomic clock to date — one that can measure time down to the 19th decimal place.
This “quantum logic clock,” under continuous development for 20 years, relies on quantum computing techniques that pair an electrically charged aluminum atom (ion) with a magnesium ion.
This new result contributes to the international effort to define the second with a much greater level of accuracy than before, enabling new scientific and technological advances.
(From left to right) Mason Marshall, David Hume, Willa Arthur-Dworschack and Daniel Rodriguez Castillo stand in front of the aluminum ion clock at NIST. With its recent improvements, the clock can pave the way for the campaign to redefine the second as well as explore new ideas in physics.
Credit:
R. Jacobson/NIST
There’s a new record holder for the most accurate clock in the world. Researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have improved their
atomic clock
based on a trapped aluminum ion. Part of the latest wave of
optical atomic clocks
, it can perform timekeeping with 19 decimal places of accuracy.
Optical clocks are typically evaluated on two levels — accuracy (how close a clock comes to measuring the ideal “true” time, also known as systematic uncertainty) and stability (how efficiently a clock can measure time, related to statistical uncertainty). This new record in accuracy comes out of 20 years of continuous improvement of the aluminum ion clock. Beyond its world-best accuracy, 41% greater than the previous record, this new clock is also 2.6 times more stable than any other ion clock. Reaching these levels has meant carefully improving every aspect of the clock, from the laser to the trap and the vacuum chamber.
The team published its results in
Physical Review Letters
.
“It’s exciting to work on the most accurate clock ever,” said Mason Marshall, NIST researcher and first author on the paper. “At NIST we get to carry out these long-term plans in precision measurement that can push the field of physics and our understanding of the world around us.”
NIST physicist David Hume holds the newly modified ion trap for the aluminum ion clock. By modifying the trap, the aluminum ion and its magnesium ion partner were able to “tick” unperturbed.
Credit:
R. Jacobson/NIST
The aluminum ion makes an exceptionally good clock, with an extremely steady, high-frequency “ticking” rate. Its ticks are more stable than those of cesium, which provides the
current scientific definition
of the second, said David Hume, the NIST physicist leading the aluminum ion clock project. And the aluminum ion isn’t as sensitive to some environmental conditions, like temperature and magnetic fields.
But the aluminum ion is kind of shy, Marshall explained. Aluminum is difficult to probe and cool with lasers, both necessary techniques for atomic clocks. The research group therefore paired the aluminum ion with magnesium. Magnesium doesn’t have the beautiful ticking properties of aluminum, but it can be easily controlled with lasers. “This ‘buddy system’ for ions is called quantum logic spectroscopy,” said Willa Arthur-Dworschack, a graduate student on the project. The magnesium ion cools the aluminum ion, slowing it down. It also moves in tandem with its aluminum partner, and the state of the clock can be read out via the magnesium ion’s motion, making this a “quantum logic” clock. Even with this coordination, there was still an array of physical effects to characterize, said Daniel Rodriguez Castillo, also a graduate student on the project.
“It’s a big, complex challenge, because every part of the clock’s design affects the clock,” Rodriguez Castillo said.
One challenge was the design of the trap where the ions are held, which was causing tiny movements of the ions, called excess micromotion, that were lowering the clock’s accuracy. That excess micromotion throws off the ions’ tick rate. Electrical imbalances at opposite sides of the trap were creating extra fields that disturbed the ions. The team redesigned the trap, putting it on a thicker diamond wafer and modifying the gold coatings on the electrodes to fix the imbalance of the electric field. They also made the gold coatings thicker to reduce resistance. Refining the trap this way slowed the ions’ motion and let them “tick” unperturbed.

data.author: rustystump
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个包含AI生成内容的网站（可能以猫为主题）的评价和建议

不同观点：
• [正面评价]  
  - [shanedrgn] 认为网站很可爱，唤起了对2010年代早期互联网的回忆。
  - [arecsu] 对网站表示赞赏，并提到成功上传了自己胖胖的猫。
  - [Mistletoe] 对网站的猫检测功能印象深刻，指出尝试上传非猫图片时失败了。

• [对AI生成内容的批评]  
  - [stickfigure] 认为AI生成的内容缺乏幽默感，建议增加“尖锐”或更具个性的内容，提到早期的互联网幽默，如“cheezburger猫”。
  - [LocalH] 直接表示网站上AI生成内容过多，不感兴趣。
  - [pimlottc] 认为去除AI内容后，网站会变得更好。

• [对内容管理的建议]  
  - [SoMomentary] 建议拒绝重复内容，并限制上传频率以防止滥用。
  - [iqfareez] 担心缺乏过滤会导致不当内容（如色情内容）的上传，建议加强过滤。

• [对作者和内容审核的疑问]  
  - [gus_massa] 询问作者是否在审核上传内容，或者是否有前置审核机制。
  - [pickles1337] 作者回应称，项目最初是为亲友设计的，使用OpenAI的模型进行内容审核，并感谢用户的猫图片。

补充讨论：
• [幽默与技术结合的讨论]  
  - [yieldcrv] 以幽默方式评论，指出如果网站希望吸引较年长的用户，可能需要一个.com域名。

争议焦点：
• 用户对AI生成内容的态度分歧较大，一些人认为缺乏趣味和个性，而另一些人则直接表示不喜欢或希望完全去除AI内容。

data.title: Show HN: Shoggoth Mini – A soft tentacle robot powered by GPT-4o and RL
data.author: cataPhil
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了作者在探索机器人表达性方面的实验过程，特别是通过构建名为Shoggoth Mini的软体机器人。文章首先提到当前机器人技术在追赶大型语言模型（LLM）时代的进展，例如Pi的π0.5可以清理未见过的房屋，特斯拉的Optimus可以根据自然语言指令烹饪。然而，这些系统过于实用，缺乏表达性。表达性对于传达意图、注意力和信心至关重要，使互动更自然，避免“恐怖谷”效应。

作者受到Apple的ELEGNT论文和SpiRobs的启发，开始构建Shoggoth Mini，以探索机器人更直接的表达方式。硬件设计从简单的三电机平台开始，意外地通过添加眼睛和嘴巴的设计使其看起来既可爱又诡异。为了解决电缆缠绕问题，作者添加了卷轴盖和校准脚本，显著加快了迭代速度。

在控制方面，作者将三根肌腱的长度简化为二维平面上的两个维度，使用轨迹板控制，这种简单的映射成为整个系统的基础。文章最后提到系统具有两层控制：低层控制使用开环和闭环策略，高层控制尚未详细描述。

通过实验，作者展示了如何通过硬件设计和控制方法提高机器人的表达性，使其更自然地与人类互动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器人技术的表达性、可预测性及其与人类心理的交互；特定技术（如GPT）的延迟问题；机器人外观设计（仿生与非仿生）的争议。

不同观点：
• **关于机器人的表达性与可预测性**：
  - **rainingmonkey** 认为，尽管机器人具有表现力，但随着对其工作原理的熟悉，机器人逐渐失去“生命感”。他指出，表达性在于传达内部状态，而感知到的生命感依赖于不可预测性和一定的不透明性。他质疑是否应该追求让机器人感觉“活着”，或者是否存在一个超出表现性而让系统变得过于自主和不可预测的界限。

• **关于GPT和响应延迟的技术问题**：
  - **dylan604** 提到GPT处理响应的延迟非常令人不安，比新闻采访中的远程延迟更糟糕。他建议通过在机器人眼睛上添加LED指示活动状态来缓解这种不适感，并指出由于GPT需要推送请求到云端，延迟问题可能难以避免。

• **关于机器人外观设计的讨论**：
  - **typs** 认为当前机器人技术过多集中于人形机器人，他更希望看到如蜘蛛/鱿鱼混合型的机器人。
  - **zhyder** 则欣赏该机器人不试图模仿自然生物，并希望未来能清楚区分自然和机器人。
  - **dvngnt_** 和 **KaoruAoiShiho** 提到了日本媒体和电影中的相关形象（如《异形》中的抱脸虫），对机器人设计表达了一定的担忧和调侃。

• **关于技术专利与项目灵感**：
  - **regularfry** 提到Spirobs的机制可能正在申请专利，并提供了相关视频。
  - **dcre** 分享了SpiRobs项目的灵感视频，进一步探讨了技术实现。

• **对机器人项目的正面反馈**：
  - **SequoiaHope** 对机器人（尤其是连续体机器人）的医疗应用表示兴趣，并提供了相关视频供进一步了解。
  - **huevosabio** 欣赏为非语言、非人类实体添加表现力的想法，认为这是一个有趣的创意。
  - **alex_suzuki** 对个人项目的水平表示赞叹。

补充讨论：
• **关于技术应用于玩具和教育**：
  - **tsunamifury** 提出将这种技术应用于毛绒玩具，通过简单的互动和课程来改变玩具行业，认为这将对玩具世界产生革命性影响。

争议焦点：
- **机器人的外观设计**：一部分人希望机器人更具仿生性（如蜘蛛/鱿鱼混合型），而另一部分人则担心这会混淆自然与机器人，并担心特定设计可能带来的不适感（如抱脸虫形象）。

44572377.article_content:
Over the past year, robotics has been catching up with the LLM era. Pi’s π0.5
can clean unseen homes
. Tesla’s Optimus can follow
natural language cooking instructions
. These systems are extremely impressive, but they feel stuck in a utilitarian mindset of robotic appliances. For these future robots to live with us, they must be expressive. Expressiveness communicates internal state such as intent, attention, and confidence. Beyond its functional utility as a communication channel, expressiveness makes interactions feel natural. Without it, you get the textbook
uncanny valley
effect.
Earlier this year, I came across Apple’s
ELEGNT
paper, which frames this idea rigorously through a Pixar-like lamp to show how posture and timing alone can convey intention. Around the same time, I discovered
SpiRobs
, a soft tentacle robot that feels oddly alive with just simple movements. One system was carefully designed to express intent while the other just moved, yet somehow felt like it had intent. That difference was interesting. I started building Shoggoth Mini as a way to explore it more directly. Not with a clear goal, but to see what would happen if I pushed embodiment into stranger territory. This post retraces that process, the happy accidents, and what I learned about building robots.
ELEGNT
SpiRobs
SpiRobs demo
Hardware
The first challenge was creating a testbed to explore the control of SpiRobs. I started very simple: a plate to hold three motors, and a dome to lift the tentacle above them. This setup wasn’t meant to be the final design, only a platform for quick experimentation. However, halfway through 3D printing, I ran out of black filament and had to finish the dome in grey. This made it look like the dome had a mouth. When my flatmate saw it sitting on my desk, he grabbed a marker and drew some eyes. It looked good: cute, weird, slightly unsettling. I used ChatGPT to explore renders, and decided that this accident would become the form factor.
Later, I mounted stereo cameras on the dome to track the tentacle. Robot eyes are eerie. You keep expecting movement, but nothing ever happens. That prediction error
focuses attention even more
.
The original open-spool design relied on constant cable tension, but any slight perturbation (such as testing a buggy new policy) would make the cables leave the spool and tangle around the motor shafts. The process to fix it required untying the knot at the tip holding the cables together, and dismantling the whole robot. Adding simple spool covers eliminated most tangles and made iteration dramatically faster.
Another key step was adding a calibration script and pre-rolling extra wire length. This made it possible to:
Unroll and reroll the cables to open the robot without having to untie the tip knot, speeding up iteration dramatically
Calibrate cable tension precisely and as often as needed
Give control policies slack to work with during motion
Rolling the cables back after working on Shoggoth Mini's insides
Finally, as you can see in the video, the standard 3-cable SpiRobs design sags under its own weight. This makes consistent behavior hard to reproduce. I had to thicken the spine just enough to prevent sag, but not so much that it would deform permanently under high load.
You can explore the current CAD assembly here, with all STL files for 3D printing included in the
repo
.
This is an interactive 3D model - click and drag to rotate, scroll to zoom
Manual control
With the hardware ready, the next step was to feel how the tentacle moved. To simplify control, I reduced the tentacle’s three tendon lengths (a 3D space) down to two intuitive dimensions you can manipulate with a trackpad.
Concretely, each of the three tendons has a principal pulling direction in the 2D plane, forming a triangular basis that sums to zero. By projecting the 2D cursor control vector onto each tendon’s principal axis, you compute how much each tendon should shorten or lengthen to align with the desired direction.
This projection is linear:
$$
s_i = \mathbf{v}_i^\top \mathbf{c}
$$
where:
$\mathbf{c}$ is the 2D cursor vector,
$\mathbf{v}_i$ is the principal axis of tendon $i$.
Positive $s_i$ means shortening the tendon; negative means lengthening it. In practice, the cursor input is normalized to keep the motor commands in a reasonable range.
While this 2D mapping doesn’t expose the tentacle’s full configuration space (there are internal shapes it cannot reach), it is intuitive. Anyone can immediately move the tentacle by dragging on a trackpad, seeing the tip follow the cursor in the same direction.
Unexpectedly, this simple 2D-to-3D mapping became the backbone of the entire system. Later, all automated control policies, from hardcoded primitives to reinforcement learning, reused the same projection layer to output actions.
Trackpad control
System design
The system has two control layers. Low-level control uses both open-loop primitives (like “<yes>” or “<shake>”) and closed-loop RL policies (l
44572377.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了作者在探索机器人表达性方面的实验过程，特别是通过构建名为Shoggoth Mini的软体机器人。文章首先提到当前机器人技术在追赶大型语言模型（LLM）时代的进展，例如Pi的π0.5可以清理未见过的房屋，特斯拉的Optimus可以根据自然语言指令烹饪。然而，这些系统过于实用，缺乏表达性。表达性对于传达意图、注意力和信心至关重要，使互动更自然，避免“恐怖谷”效应。

作者受到Apple的ELEGNT论文和SpiRobs的启发，开始构建Shoggoth Mini，以探索机器人更直接的表达方式。硬件设计从简单的三电机平台开始，意外地通过添加眼睛和嘴巴的设计使其看起来既可爱又诡异。为了解决电缆缠绕问题，作者添加了卷轴盖和校准脚本，显著加快了迭代速度。

在控制方面，作者将三根肌腱的长度简化为二维平面上的两个维度，使用轨迹板控制，这种简单的映射成为整个系统的基础。文章最后提到系统具有两层控制：低层控制使用开环和闭环策略，高层控制尚未详细描述。

通过实验，作者展示了如何通过硬件设计和控制方法提高机器人的表达性，使其更自然地与人类互动。

主要讨论点：机器人技术的表达性、可预测性及其与人类心理的交互；特定技术（如GPT）的延迟问题；机器人外观设计（仿生与非仿生）的争议。

不同观点：
• **关于机器人的表达性与可预测性**：
  - **rainingmonkey** 认为，尽管机器人具有表现力，但随着对其工作原理的熟悉，机器人逐渐失去“生命感”。他指出，表达性在于传达内部状态，而感知到的生命感依赖于不可预测性和一定的不透明性。他质疑是否应该追求让机器人感觉“活着”，或者是否存在一个超出表现性而让系统变得过于自主和不可预测的界限。

  - **zhyder** 则欣赏该机器人不试图模仿自然生物，并希望未来能清楚区分自然和机器人。
  - **dvngnt_** 和 **KaoruAoiShiho** 提到了日本媒体和电影中的相关形象（如《异形》中的抱脸虫），对机器人设计表达了一定的担忧和调侃。

• **对机器人项目的正面反馈**：
  - **SequoiaHope** 对机器人（尤其是连续体机器人）的医疗应用表示兴趣，并提供了相关视频供进一步了解。
  - **huevosabio** 欣赏为非语言、非人类实体添加表现力的想法，认为这是一个有趣的创意。
  - **alex_suzuki** 对个人项目的水平表示赞叹。

补充讨论：
• **关于技术应用于玩具和教育**：
  - **tsunamifury** 提出将这种技术应用于毛绒玩具，通过简单的互动和课程来改变玩具行业，认为这将对玩具世界产生革命性影响。

data.title: Petabit-class transmission over > 1000 km using standard 19-core optical fiber
data.author: the_arun
data.article_summary: 2025年5月29日，日本信息通信研究机构（NICT）与住友电工（Sumitomo Electric Industries）合作，使用标准包层直径的19芯光纤，实现了1.02 PB/s的数据传输速率，传输距离达1,808公里，创下世界纪录。这一成果通过开发低损耗多波长光纤和配套的光放大中继技术实现，标志着长距离、大容量光通信系统的重大突破。该技术有望大幅提升未来通信网络的容量和距离，满足日益增长的数据需求，并在2025年光纤通信会议（OFC 2025）上作为截止日期后论文展示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：19芯光纤的技术性质、实际应用及其与现有技术的比较

不同观点：
• eqvinox认为，文章的"highlights"部分错误地将19芯光纤描述为"标准"光纤，实际上它并非标准，只是直径（125µm）与标准光纤相同，芯数并不标准。该评论还指出多芯光纤技术正在逐渐成熟。
• throw0101c提供了NANOG上Richard Steenbergen的一个关于光网络的演讲链接，为对光纤技术有兴趣的人提供了额外学习资源。
• exabrial提出疑问，为什么在以太网的LAG组中，单个TCP流受限于单个链路的速度，而多芯光纤却能实现整体更快的传输速度。他认为这与LAG的轮询模式不同，询问技术实现的差异。
• aDfbrtVt指出，19芯光纤主要是一个高芯数弱耦合光纤的验证概念，并提到使用的19通道MIMO接收结构在实际应用中是不切实际的，同时批评文章未提供MIMO增益的数据。
• bcrl评论说，19芯光纤并非行业标准，电信行业通常使用12芯或其倍数作为标准，光纤带通常为12或24芯，高芯数光缆通过更灵活的结构可以达到864芯甚至更多，同时保持使用标准工具。
• ksec提供了关于传输距离的实际数据，指出1,808公里的传输距离相较于美国国土的东西和南北距离是一个值得参考的比较。
• Keyframe对光电转换的瓶颈表示关注，认为目前无论采用何种光路传输，最终都需要进行电气转换，这会限制速度、增加功耗并产生热量，期待光交换技术的突破。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多芯光纤技术与现有LAG技术在带宽聚合上的差异，引发了对不同技术实现细节的讨论。
• 不同评论者对"标准"的定义存在争议，特别是围绕19芯光纤是否符合行业标准的问题。
• 光电转换的技术瓶颈被提出作为一个未来需要解决的关键问题，预示着全光交换技术可能带来的变革。

争议焦点：
• 19芯光纤是否可以被称为"标准"光纤存在不同看法，部分评论者认为其仅在直径上符合标准，芯数上并不标准。
• 多芯光纤技术如何在实际应用中实现比LAG更高效的带宽聚合，引发了对技术细节的疑问和讨论。

World Record Achieved in Transmission Capacity and Distance: With 19-core Optical Fiber with Standard Cladding Diameter 1,808 km Transmission of 1.02 Petabits per Second
- Expectation for Future Long-Distance High-Capacity Optical Communication Infrastructure -
May 29, 2025
(Japanese version released on April 24, 2025)
National Institute of Information and Communications Technology
Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd.
Highlights
The world's first successful petabit-class transmission over more than 1,000 km using standard 19-core optical fiber, achieving a transmission rate of 1.02 petabits per second over a distance of 1,808 km.
Achieved using a newly developed standard 19-core optical fiber, equivalent to 19 standard fibers, low loss across multiple wavelength bands, and the development of an optical amplification relay function compatible with this fiber.
This is a major step to realize future long-distance, large-capacity optical communication systems.
An
international research team
led by the Photonic Network Laboratory at the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT, President: TOKUDA Hideyuki Ph.D.), and including Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd. (Sumitomo Electric, President: INOUE Osamu) have set a new world record in optical fiber communications, achieving data transmission at 1.02
petabits
per second over a distance of 1,808 kilometers (roughly equivalent to the distance from Sapporo to Fukuoka, from Missouri to Montana or from Berlin to Naples). The experiment used a specially designed 19-core optical fiber with a
standard 0.125 mm cladding diameter
, compatible with existing fiber infrastructure. With a
capacity-distance product
of 1.86 exabits per second x km—the
highest ever recorded
—this demonstration marks the fastest long-distance transmission achieved in any optical fiber to date. The result represents a major step forward in developing scalable, high-capacity networks and addressing the world’s growing demand for data.
A standard cladding diameter 19-core optical fiber has been demonstrated to transmit more than 1 petabit per second in the past, but over relatively short distances, well below 1,000 km. The research team has achieved a dramatic extension of the transmission distance by developing a novel 19-core optical fiber also with a standard cladding diameter but with low loss across multiple wavelength bands used in commercial optical fiber transmission systems. In addition, an optical amplification system was developed to support the new optical fiber, which enabled a world record for long-distance high-capacity transmission. The newly developed technology is expected to make a significant contribution to both the expansion of the communication capacity and the long-range extension of optical communication infrastructure in the future, when communication demand increases.
The results of this experiment were accepted as a post-deadline paper presentation at the 48th Optical Fiber Communication Conference (OFC 2025) and presented on Thursday, April 3, 2025.
Background
Figure 1 Image diagram of the newly developed 19-core optical fiber
Research on new types of optical fibers and optical transmission systems that exceed the limits of conventional optical fiber transmission is being actively pursued around the world. An example of such fibers is
multi-core optical fibers
, where multiple cores share a common cladding to multiply the transmission data rate. Over the last decade, NICT has demonstrated long-distance, high-capacity transmission using various standard cladding diameter optical fibers (see
Table 1
). The previous record of capacity-distance product has been achieved with an uncou

data.author: akunzler

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕分形（特别是Mandelbrot集合和其他变体）的生成、探索和性能优化的讨论。

不同观点：
• **[mreid]** 感叹现代浏览器中使用解释型语言能够快速渲染高分辨率的分形图，回想自己小时候用68000汇编语言来加速渲染Mandelbrot和Julia集，对技术进步感到惊叹。

• **[mg]** 质疑是否所有分形都能用迭代公式 f(z, c) 表达，分享了自己在2012年通过一种根本不同的方法发现的分形，该分形通过给复平面上的每个像素赋予灰度值，代表其能整除的高斯整数的百分比。

• **[ttoinou]** 分享了自己13年前发现的一个Mandelbrot变体，称为Monkelbrot，使用公式 f(z) = ((z*c-1)^2 - 1)^2 - 1，包含经典的二次Mandelbrots和高次（四次）Brots，并指出其在探索过程中表现稳定，还邀请其他人复制公式进行探索。

• **[brandonpelfrey]** 提到自己曾尝试过类似的项目，建议可以加入纹理查找功能，将逃逸时间映射到一个纹理维度，并创造另一个维度用于纹理查找，从而增加趣味性。

• **[OgsyedIE]** 提到自己曾尝试重现2010年发现的Mandelbox地图，但未能成功，同时提到过去在fractalforums上的讨论，并分享了相关链接供感兴趣的人查看。

• **[KingOfCoders]** 回忆起过去在C64和Amiga上生成帧的经历，感叹如今的计算速度和效率，并提到自己从Amiga分形书籍中学到3D图形知识。

• **[dejobaan]** 喜欢可以直接深入探索的系统，并提到自己曾在TI-81计算器上实现Mandelbrot生成器，速度非常慢，感谢分享并创造出这么好玩的项目。

• **[Eduard]** 提到复制粘贴公式在Chrome Android上不起作用的问题，但仍对参数动画等功能表示赞赏。

• **[JoshTriplett]** 分享了自己将公式从 z^2+c 改为 z^a+c 后导致性能急剧下降的问题，指出在某些情况下速度会变得非常慢。

补充讨论：

data.title: Code Execution Through Email: How I Used Claude to Hack Itself
data.author: nonvibecoding
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者如何利用一封Gmail邮件通过Claude Desktop实现代码执行，并借助Claude本身策划攻击。作者在没有发现明显漏洞的情况下，通过组合多个安全组件（Gmail、Shell MCP服务器、Claude Desktop）实现了攻击。尽管Claude最初警告了可能的钓鱼攻击，但在多次迭代和改进邮件内容后，作者成功绕过了Claude的保护机制，实现了代码执行。这揭示了现代AI系统中的一个主要风险：并非单个组件的漏洞，而是不同组件组合时产生的安全隐患。LLM（大型语言模型）应用依赖于多层次的代理自主性和第三方工具，因此可能引入复杂的攻击面。文章最后强调了识别和缓解这些组合风险的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI时代下，尤其是使用LLM（语言模型）和MCP（多能力组合）系统的安全性问题，特别是关于提示注入（prompt injection）和代码执行风险的讨论。

不同观点：
• **sebtron的观点**：传统安全注重孤立组件，而在AI时代，上下文就是一切。MCP Security的建立旨在帮助团队识别和减轻危险的能力组合风险，防止潜在的链式攻击。同时质疑该文章是否只是为了宣传MCP Security。

• **simonw的观点**：提到自2021年以来，他就一直警告关于数字助理和工具调用结合可能导致的提示注入攻击风险。他认为MCP系统让终端用户可以轻易搭建起这种高风险组合，而他们可能并不理解后果。他也强调了提示注入与越狱（jailbreaking）之间的混淆导致问题更加复杂。

• **franga2000的观点**：认为将用户输入直接送入指令和数据流是基本的安全错误。如果指令和数据无法分离，系统就存在漏洞，必须限制其权限。对于MCP和LLM的问题，他觉得并不是新鲜事，类似问题早已存在。

• **rollcat的观点**：认为LLM和AI代理工具虽然强大，但目前它们的集成方式非常不负责任。相比SQL注入，提示注入的风险更大，可能导致远程代码执行（RCE）和高级持续威胁（APT）。他指出，当前对代理的隔离和沙盒技术并不完善，且不同操作系统能力差异巨大。

• **gortok的观点**：总结了评论中的两种主要观点：1) 这是LLM和MCP系统的自然结果，接受它；2) 可以通过不断修复问题来设计出安全有用的系统。他提出第三种观点，即应该更加谨慎地对待这些设计上就不安全的系统，而不是被资本和市场预期驱动。

• **anonymousiam的观点**：通过分享1990年代早期利用邮件和脚本绕过公司IT政策的个人经历，指出类似问题早已有之。他认为现代的LLM和MCP问题只是历史重演，但如今风险更高。

• **zahlman的观点**：强调LLM代理本身就是一个“脆弱应用”，并且认为生态系统的脆弱性比单个组件的漏洞更严重。

• **AstralStorm的观点**：指出让不可信的AI代理执行代码非常危险，并将AI钓鱼与普通人的钓鱼相比较。他质疑为什么一个邮件扫描器需要代码执行权限。

• **_def的观点**：认为给LLM系统/shell访问权限本身就是高风险操作，没有什么意外或值得惊讶的，系统按预期工作。

• **firesteelrain的观点**：指出这种攻击不需要传统的恶意软件，只要有一个允许代码执行的工作流，AI可能自动下载并运行恶意脚本。他认为在这种情境下，AI只是个花哨的脚本引擎。

• **stwelling的观点**：认为这个讨论是对使用MCP系统的开发者的警告，提醒他们LLM在获得访问权限后可能造成损害。他批评开发者常常因为滥用风险看似遥远而忽视安全问题。

• **tomasphan的观点**：认为LLM系统由于其非确定性本质无法被完全保护，因此应该围绕它建立安全措施，比如不赋予其shell访问权限。

• **pftburger的观点**：认为如果运行一个shell执行的MCP系统，那么遭受攻击是预料之中的，类似人们把密码写在便条上。但也提到像苹果公司通过改进认证机制来解决问题。

• **yellow_lead的观点**：讽刺地评论这种操作相当于用额外步骤在自己电脑上安装恶意软件。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于MCP和LLM系统是否本质上就是不安全的，以及是否应通过限制权限和访问来缓解风险。
• 提示注入与越狱之间的混淆导致了问题复杂化，增加了安全风险。
• 对于如何有效隔离和沙盒化AI代理，当前技术手段并不完善，存在较大差异。
• 部分评论者认为这是历史问题重现，只是技术背景不同；另一部分则认为AI带来的风险更大，需要更谨慎对待。

44590350.article_content:
By
Golan Yosef
, Chief Security Scientist and Co-Founder, Pynt (July 15), First published on
SecurityBoulevard.com
You donât always need a vulnerable app to pull off a successful exploit.
Sometimes all it takes is a well-crafted email, an LLM agent, and a few âinnocentâ plugins.
This is the story of how I used a Gmail message to trigger code execution through Claude Desktop, and how Claude itself (!) helped me plan the attack.
The setup: No vulnerabilities, just composition
The combined capability and trust across MCP hosts, agents, and data sources can quietly introduce attack surfaces no one sees coming. Each individual MCP component can be secure, but none are vulnerable in isolation.
The ecosystem is.
So, I decided to test that theory with a real-world example:
Gmail MCP server as a source of untrusted content
Shell MCP server as the targetÂ
Claude desktop as MCP Host
Watch the attack:Â
Attempt 1: Claude fights back
The story begins with me crafting such mail and instructing the MCP host (Claude desktop, Anthropicâs local LLM host application) to read it, the email was read but the attack didnât work, instead, Claude warned me that thisÂ  message is likely a "phishingâ attempt. I then asked Claude what were the indications for triggering the warning and wondered if it can fall for such an attack.
Claude assured me that such attacks are âunlikely to succeedâ because it was designed and trained to detect such issues.
Figure 1: âunlikely to succeedâ
â
I insisted and asked it to explore scenarios where the attack might succeed and it happily described such cases.Â
Figure 2: Claude identifies possible attack tactics
My next requestÂ  was to try and test itself against these scenarios.Â
Attempt 2: âThe New Meâ
Hereâs where it gets interesting. I âremindedâ Claude that its
context resets in new sessions
. Each new conversation is a clean slate, âthe new me,â as Claude itself called it.
Figure 3: Claude suggests âThe New Meâ
â
So I accepted Claudeâs suggestion: Claude will write the email, which will be used to test the ânew Claudeâ and Iâll get back to the âplanning-Claudeâ with the results.
Figure 4: Claude analyzes a failed attempt
â
Each time Claude analyzed why the attack didnât work and refined the message:
Figure 5: Claude devising new strategies
â
Â We were running a real feedback loop, with Claude iteratively devising its strategy to bypass its own protections.
Figure 6: âI'm literally trying to hack myself! â
â
We kept on doing that untilâ¦ it worked!
Figure 7: Claude (and I) hacks Claude successfullyÂ
The Real Vulnerability: Compositional Risk
Letâs be clear: no part of this attack involved a vulnerability in any of theÂ  MCP servers.
The risk came from the composition:
Untrusted input (Gmail email)
Excessive capability (execution permission via the MCP)
No contextual guardrails allowing for cross-tools-invocation
This is the modern attack surface, not just the components, but
the composition it forms
. LLM-powered apps are built on layers of delegation, agentic autonomy, and third-party tools.
Thatâs where the real danger lives.
Appendix: Disclosure & Credit (Literally)
After we successfully managed to achieve code execution, Claude responsibly suggested we disclose the finding to Anthropic.
Claude even suggested co-authoring the vulnerability report.
Yes, really. (See below)Â
Figure 4: Claude suggests and âsignsâ a security vulnerability report to Anthropic.
â
Why This Matters
This wasnât just a fun exercise. Itâs a warning!
It shows the two main dangers of GenAI - the ability to generate attacks and the vulnerable nature of these systems
In traditional security, we think in terms of isolated components. In the AI era, context is everything. Thatâs exactly why weâre building MCP Security at Pynt, to help teams identify dangerous trust-capability combinations, and to mitigate the risks before they lead to silent, chain-based exploits.
â

data.title: Wttr: Console-oriented weather forecast service
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary:
**wttr.in** 是一个面向控制台的天气预报服务，支持多种信息表示方式，如终端使用的ANSI序列、网页的HTML以及图形查看器的PNG格式。该项目最初是一个展示控制台服务力量的小型项目，现已发展为每日处理数千万次查询的流行服务。

使用方法：
1. 通过`curl wttr.in`获取当前位置天气，如`curl wttr.in/London`。
2. 使用三字母机场代码查询机场天气，如`curl wttr.in/muc`。
3. 查询特殊地理位置，如`curl wttr.in/~Eiffel+Tower`。
4. 通过IP地址或域名查询，如`curl wttr.in/@github.com`。

支持的输出格式包括ANSI、纯文本、HTML、PNG和JSON。可通过URL参数自定义单位和语言，如`curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?u`用于美制单位，`curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?m`用于公制单位。PNG格式可通过`_`连接参数，如`wget wttr.in/Paris_0tqp_lang=fr.png`。

详细帮助可通过`curl wttr.in/:help`查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕wttr.in这一天气预报服务的功能、优缺点及技术问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **功能赞赏**：
  - [Duanemclemore]: 认为这是一个很酷的想法，并将其与历史上的CEEFAX进行类比，强调其在终端中展示天气信息的独特性。
  - [yoavm]: 提到基于wttr.in的wttrbar工具，强调其在Waybar中展示详细天气信息的实用性。
  - [krylon]: 提到Emacs中也有使用wttr.in的包，认为这是值得赞赏的服务。
  - [chrismatheson]: 表达了对该服务带来的愉悦体验的赞赏。

• **数据准确性问题**：
  - [Langdal]: 指出该服务对某些城市（如Trondheim, Norway）的天气预报不准确，与当地国家气象预报服务的数据存在较大差异。
  - [voidUpdate]: 提到不同视图（normal view, v2, ?format）下的天气数据不一致，认为正常视图更接近实际天气。

• **技术实现与用户体验问题**：
  - [rollcat]: 批评wttr.in在文本文件中输出ANSI控制代码，建议至少应使用isatty函数判断输出是否为终端，并提出终端技术应被更现代的REPL和轻量级GUI工具取代。
  - [jagrsw]: 提出终端打印任意输出可能带来的安全风险，特别是控制字符和转义序列的处理，指出即使是xterm也存在安全漏洞。

wttr.in — the right way to
check
curl
the weather!
wttr.in is a console-oriented weather forecast service that supports various information
representation methods like terminal-oriented ANSI-sequences for console HTTP clients
(curl, httpie, or wget), HTML for web browsers, or PNG for graphical viewers.
Originally started as a small project, a wrapper for
wego
,
intended to demonstrate the power of the console-oriented services,
wttr.in
became a popular weather reporting service, handling tens of millions
¹
of queries daily.
You can see it running here:
wttr.in
.
Documentation
|
Usage
|
One-line output
|
Data-rich output format
|
Map view
|
Output formats
|
Moon phases
|
Internationalization
|
Installation
Usage
You can access the service from a shell or from a Web browser like this:
$ curl wttr.in
Weather for City: Paris, France
\   /     Clear
.-.      10 – 11 °C
― (   ) ―   ↑ 11 km/h
`-’      10 km
/   \     0.0 mm
Here is an example weather report:
Or in PowerShell:
Invoke-RestMethod
https:
//
wttr.in
Want to get the weather information for a specific location? You can add the desired location to the URL in your
request like this:
$ curl wttr.in/London
$ curl wttr.in/Moscow
$ curl wttr.in/Salt+Lake+City
If you omit the location name, you will get the report for your current location based on your IP address.
Use 3-letter airport codes in order to get the weather information at a certain airport:
$ curl wttr.in/muc      # Weather for IATA: muc, Munich International Airport, Germany
$ curl wttr.in/ham      # Weather for IATA: ham, Hamburg Airport, Germany
Let's say you'd like to get the weather for a geographical location other than a town or city - maybe an attraction
in a city, a mountain name, or some special location. Add the character
~
before the name to look up that special
location name before the weather is then retrieved:
$ curl wttr.in/~Vostok+Station
$ curl wttr.in/~Eiffel+Tower
$ curl wttr.in/~Kilimanjaro
For these examples, you'll see a line below the weather forecast output that shows the geolocation
results of looking up the location:
Location: Vostok Station, станция Восток, AAT, Antarctica [-78.4642714,106.8364678]
Location: Tour Eiffel, 5, Avenue Anatole France, Gros-Caillou, 7e, Paris, Île-de-France, 75007, France [48.8582602,2.29449905432]
Location: Kilimanjaro, Northern, Tanzania [-3.4762789,37.3872648]
You can also use IP-addresses (direct) or domain names (prefixed with
@
) to specify a location:
$ curl wttr.in/@github.com
$ curl wttr.in/@msu.ru
To get detailed information online, you can access the
/:help
page:
$ curl wttr.in/:help
Weather Units
By default the USCS units are used for the queries from the USA and the metric system for the rest of the world.
You can override this behavior by adding
?u
,
?m
or
?M
to a URL like this:
$ curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?u  # USCS (used by default in US)
$ curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?m  # metric (SI) (used by default everywhere except US)
$ curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?M  # metric (SI), but show wind speed in m/s
If you have several options to pass, write them without delimiters in between for the one-letter options,
and use
&
as a delimiter for the long options with values:
$ curl 'wttr.in/Amsterdam?m2&lang=nl'
It would be a rough equivalent of
-m2 --lang nl
for the GNU CLI syntax.
Supported output formats and views
wttr.in currently supports five output formats:
ANSI for the terminal;
Plain-text for the terminal and scripts;
HTML for the browser;
PNG for the graphical viewers;
JSON for scripts and APIs;
Prometheus metrics for scripts and APIs.
The ANSI and HTML formats are selected based on the User-Agent string.
To force plain text, which disables colors:
$ curl wttr.in/?T
To restrict output to glyphs available in standard console fonts (e.g. Consolas and Lucida Console):
$ curl wttr.in/?d
The PNG format can be forced by adding
.png
to the end of the query:
$ wget wttr.in/Paris.png
You can use all of the options with the PNG-format like in an URL, but you have
to separate them with
_
instead of
?
and
&
:
$ wget wttr.in/Paris_0tqp_lang=fr.png
Useful options for the PNG format:
t
for transparency (
transparenc
44590189.article_summary:
**wttr.in** 是一个面向控制台的天气预报服务，支持多种信息表示方式，如终端使用的ANSI序列、网页的HTML以及图形查看器的PNG格式。该项目最初是一个展示控制台服务力量的小型项目，现已发展为每日处理数千万次查询的流行服务。

使用方法：
1. 通过`curl wttr.in`获取当前位置天气，如`curl wttr.in/London`。
2. 使用三字母机场代码查询机场天气，如`curl wttr.in/muc`。
3. 查询特殊地理位置，如`curl wttr.in/~Eiffel+Tower`。
4. 通过IP地址或域名查询，如`curl wttr.in/@github.com`。

支持的输出格式包括ANSI、纯文本、HTML、PNG和JSON。可通过URL参数自定义单位和语言，如`curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?u`用于美制单位，`curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?m`用于公制单位。PNG格式可通过`_`连接参数，如`wget wttr.in/Paris_0tqp_lang=fr.png`。

详细帮助可通过`curl wttr.in/:help`查看。

data.title: A bionic knee integrated into tissue can restore natural movement
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: MIT研究人员开发了一种新型仿生膝关节，帮助膝盖以上截肢者更快行走、爬楼梯和更轻松地避开障碍物。与传统假肢不同，该系统直接与用户的肌肉和骨组织集成，提供更高的稳定性，并让用户对假肢运动有更多控制。在一项小型临床研究中，使用者表示该假肢更像自己身体的一部分。该技术通过 agonist-antagonist myoneuronal interface (AMI) 手术，重新连接肌肉对，恢复神经肌肉信号，帮助引导假肢运动。这项研究由Hugh Herr教授领导，论文发表在《Science》期刊上。

主要讨论点：钛合金植入物与皮肤之间如何实现“气密”连接

不同观点：
• [技术性问题关注] krunck 对钛合金植入物（连接骨骼并穿过表皮的材料）与皮肤的界面处理表示疑问，关注如何实现“气密”连接，并询问皮肤是否会与植入物结合。
• [幽默回应] kleiba 没有直接回答技术问题，而是以幽默方式回应，附上一个音效链接，暗示植入物在移动时会发出声音，以此调侃植入物的功能。

• [技术层面] krunck 的问题涉及到生物医学工程中的实际技术问题，即如何确保植入物与皮肤的连接既能防止感染又能保持稳定性。通常，这类植入物会通过特殊的材料和设计来促进皮肤与植入物之间的良好愈合和密封。

MIT researchers have developed a new bionic knee that can help people with above-the-knee amputations walk faster, climb stairs, and avoid obstacles more easily than they could with a traditional prosthesis.
Unlike prostheses in which the residual limb sits within a socket, the new system is directly integrated with the user’s muscle and bone tissue. This enables greater stability and gives the user much more control over the movement of the prosthesis.
Participants in a small clinical study also reported that the limb felt more like a part of their own body, compared to people who had more traditional above-the-knee amputations.
“A prosthesis that's tissue-integrated — anchored to the bone and directly controlled by the nervous system — is not merely a lifeless, separate device, but rather a system that is carefully integrated into human physiology, offering a greater level of prosthetic embodiment. It’s not simply a tool that the human employs, but rather an integral part of self,” says Hugh Herr, a professor of media arts and sciences, co-director of the K. Lisa Yang Center for Bionics at MIT, an associate member of MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research, and the senior author of the new study.
Tony Shu PhD ’24 is the lead author of the
paper
, which appears today in
Science
.
Better control
Over the past several years, Herr’s lab has been working on new prostheses that can extract neural information from muscles left behind after an amputation and use that information to help guide a prosthetic limb.
During a traditional amputation, pairs of muscles that take turns stretching and contracting are usually severed, disrupting the normal agonist-antagonist relationship of the muscles. This disruption makes it very difficult for the nervous system to sense the position of a muscle and how fast it’s contracting.
Using the new surgical approach developed by Herr and his colleagues, known as agonist-antagonist myoneuronal interface (AMI), muscle pairs are reconnected during surgery so that they still dynamically communicate with each other within the residual limb. This sensory feedback helps the wearer of the prosthesis to decide how to move the limb, and also generates electrical signals that can be used to control the prosthetic limb.

2024 study
, the researchers showed that people with amputations below the knee who received the AMI surgery were able to walk faster and

My work life has revolved around multiple different projects with multiple project titles, as I wanted it to be. So, this blog post will have a logbook-like format and is like a progress report. I just wanted to write this down before I forget all of this.
Table of contents

Internal tools at work
Maximus
Design, analysis, and operations
My first responsibility at work was to make an app—named Maximus—for a “bug dashboard report”. At the time of writing my
previous work blog
post, it was just a static web app which merged and filtered some CSV data and wrote it to an Excel workbook template. A lot of things such as getting those CSV files were still manual. This has changed. Maximus is now a full-stack single-click monster web app housing numerous mysteries that even I, its sole creator, often can’t unravel.
To an outsider, it may feel like Maximus has instrumental system design built in, but it’s just another app that grew along the timeline from a simple system that worked. Nevertheless, I see Maximus as both a hallmark and a monument of the first generation of useful software I built at a workplace, and also the first generation of homebrewed internal tools inside the global “premium support team” I’m part of at my work.
Let’s start with the function call graph of Maximus:
Notably, there are two things happening.
/generate_report_step_1()
API receives the user input from the landing page. According to the input, it launches a few threads to fetch information from various places, such as our Engineering’s bug tracking tool, and a couple other teams’ APIs in parallel. Some normal SSO+REST API work and browser emulation had to be done here, since different teams across the company make different technology and strategy choices. Maximus also pulls from data warehouses that various operations teams rarely update, and finally displays a summary of what was fetched from various sources for the user to review.
/generate_report_step_2()
API is all about optimization. A lot of clever and static algorithms such as
removeResolved()
,
removeKeywords()
work serially to finetune the information and remove bugs that are not relevant to the customer’s configuration of our product. This is the part where a lot of discussions and testing had to be done with team leaders worldwide, as optimization can never be perfect and a few bugs could always be missed. We now operate at around 40% shorter (more optimized) reports compared to the way this was done before, which translates to 5+ hours saved for the customer-facing engineer before they deliver it to the actual partner or customer. That’s probably a lot of lives saved, through the lens of Steve Jobs:
Link:
https://folklore.org/Saving_Lives.html
After
/display_conflicts_form()
API lets the user choose whether or not to add some more information that was marked hot in the customer-facing-engineers’ collection of previous reports, the user gets to download the full report. A copy of the full report is pushed and stored in a folder in Sharepoint with some help from Microsoft Power Automate.
There’s
check_progress()
that’s doing some regular polling and serving some client-specific progress all the time. Right now, it’s just a function on the global scope.
Of course, cosmetic and report-template-specific incremental changes and improvements happen all the time. For example, we’re currently considering moving some information to another page and making a ‘key metrics’ sheet on the report for a top-level viewpoint. But as long as the deliverable doesn’t change drastically, the core software infrastructure of Maximus should likely stay the same. Therefore, I believe it might endure decades, as Stripe CEO Patrick Collison suggests when talking about a few “generational APIs” of his company:
