44559375.article_content:
Jul 13, 2025
Task Runner Census 2025
TL;DR - Key Take-aways
GitHub Actions dominates CI/CD, Make is omnipresent, and new package managers like uv and pnpm are popular in new repos.
How and why I counted
Every software project accretes snippets of code for developers to execute that are outside the primary codebase. These are named and saved in shell scripts, configs for build tools, package managers, CI runners, and occasionally just code blocks in the README. To find out what people are actually doing in 2025, I crawled the 100,000 most starred repos on GitHub and checked what config files they had. The primary motivation was figuring out what I should support in
dela
, my delegating task runner.
The Leaderboards
Most used task runners
Of the top 100,000 starred repos, 72,804 had detectable task runners. For repo counts, y axis is the total number of repos in which a task runner was detected. For star counts, y axis is the cumulative sum of stars in the detected repos. To be included in the chart, the task runner had to appear in at least 100 repos.
Most used since 2025-01-01
Below are charts only for the repositories created since 2025-01-01 that feature in the top 100k starred repositories. 1,127 repositories made this year have made it into the top 100k most starred repos overall. To be included in the chart, the task runner also had to appear in at least 10 of those repositories.
A taxonomy of task runners
There is a continuum of tooling that can execute code, but not all executions could be considered tasks. My criteria is that the tool is meant to work with the repository and has well-known patterns that could be detected from filenames. This means that things like Python scripts and shell scripts are out because their domain of utility can’t be localized to the repository. Any code that is meant to be run by the user rather than by the developer is also out, such as arg parsers for CLI tools. GitHub Actions, on the other hand, are included because they deal with the repository and are run on behalf of the developer even if they are not typically executed locally.
Build Tool - Tools to manage caching of dependencies when compiling but allow arbitrary code execution.
make
is the prototypical example and is probably the inspiration for most tools in this and other categories.
Package Manager - Package managers like
npm
and
uv
can have a list of tasks they execute, even though it is not their primary purpose.
Easy CLI - These are tools that make it easy to create code that is callable from the shell by developers, but not meant to be distributed. Examples include
rake
and
invoke
, which turn Ruby and Python methods into tasks invokable via the shell.
Task Runner - This is a category for pure task runners that aren’t coupled to another major feature;
just
and
go-task
are examples.
CI/CD Tool - Like build tools but running on somebody else’s infrastructure and also allow arbitrary code execution.
Process Manager - Orchestrate concurrent tasks and supervise their execution. Useful for production servers like
systemd
, but also used in development like
foreman
.
Make & GitHub Actions - General Purpose Leaders
GitHub Actions
appears in 39.8% of the repositories, beating out the next best of 13.9% for
Travis CI
and 2.1% for
Circle CI
in the CI/CD category. That is an amazing victory for GitHub, because
GitHub Actions
only launched in 2019 and was free for public repositories from the start.
Travis CI
had a head start with being free for public repositories since 2011, but in 2020 switched to free for open source with manual review on a case-by-case basis only.
Circle CI
has been free for open source projects since 2014.
At 49 years old,
make
makes its presence seen in 19.0% of the repos. This is remarkable considering how much of present-day software is written in languages that don’t
need
a build step or have it provided by a special tool in their own ecosystem. I attribute part of its continued success to its ability to be used as a general-purpose task runner via the
.PHONY
build targets. Trailing it are
bazel
at 1.5% in the build tools category and
just
at just 0.4% in the task runner category.
27.2% of the repos did not have a detected task runner at all. The most popular of these is
build-your-own-x
with 392,036 stars at the time of the scan.
JavaScript ecosystem - pnpm rising
With 28.5% of all repos,
npm
is at the top of the pack in the JavaScript ecosystem and makes JS the most popular language ecosystem. In the jockeying for 2nd and 3rd place for JS package managers,
pnpm
came out from behind to land in 2nd place for new 2025 repos and 3rd place overall.
pnpm
is being used in 22.9% of all new JS repos made since 2025. This is a larger share than
yarn
ever had.

data.title: Open, free, and ignored: the afterlife of Symbian
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: Symbian，这个由Psion和Nokia共同开发的早期智能手机操作系统，尽管在技术上具有创新性（如EKA2微内核），并已开放源代码，但如今却被忽视。文章回顾了Symbian的发展历史及其衰落原因，包括Nokia在用户界面上的失误和Arm处理器的普及。尽管Symbian曾广泛应用于数百万设备，且拥有繁荣的第三方应用市场，但其开源版本在GitHub上几乎无人问津。相比之下，其他从头开发的操作系统项目（如Genode OS和Serenity OS）却吸引了更多关注。文章还提到其他20世纪专有操作系统的命运，如AmigaOS和BeOS，它们部分被重建或应用于新平台，而Symbian则被遗忘。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Symbian操作系统的设计、开发和消亡原因，以及与现代操作系统的比较。

不同观点：
• **pavlov**：Symbian是一个从零设计的操作系统，专为特定用例优化，但在中期假设上失算。尽管在1997年为低资源设备设计是合理的，但十年后苹果和谷歌推出的智能手机具备更强的硬件和网络支持，Symbian的效率优势反而成为劣势。Nokia在2008年试图通过增加POSIX和触屏支持来挽回局面，但为时已晚，无法与Android竞争。

• **harshaw**：作为开发者，体验不好。Symbian的 memory management 模型难以编程且容易崩溃。与Nokia合作时，遇到开发困难，Nokia对调试第三方应用的兴趣不大。总体上，早期移动操作系统竞争激烈，Symbian的消亡并不意外。

• **sunshine-o**：Symbian是最后一个开放的手机开发平台，支持Qt、JavaME等框架，旧版Skype等应用运行良好。然而，Android和iOS的兴起改变了生态，导致如今银行应用无法在Lineage和Graphene上运行，用户体验变差。

• **raverbashing**：Symbian消亡有其原因，大多数开发者认为开发过程痛苦。

• **actionfromafar**：Symbian速度快且小巧，但难以达到完全稳定。随着硬件提升，操作系统的基础稳定性变得更重要。

• **inglor_cz**：Symbian的操作系统内核速度快且高效，但学习曲线陡峭，开发工具（如Carbide.c++）差，设备兼容性差且碎片化严重。虽然内核技术出色，但整个生态系统被合理地放弃了。

• **secondcoming**：重新构建Symbian代码将是一个巨大的工程，原有的Perl构建系统和SDK可能已不再可用。不过，仍有少数开发者在继续开发Symbian。

• **fsflover**：与Symbian的消亡对比，Mobian和postmarketOS等项目却蓬勃发展，引发思考。

补充讨论：
- Symbian的开发难度和工具问题被广泛提及，尤其是内存管理和开发工具的不足。
- 不同开发者对Symbian的体验和看法各异，有的强调其技术优点，有的则批评其生态系统的不足。
- 对现代移动操作系统（如Android和iOS）的批评主要集中在封闭性和应用兼容性问题上。
- 关于Symbian消亡原因的讨论中，硬件发展和市场时机被认为是关键因素。
- 关于现代Linux移动操作系统的成功，如Mobian和postmarketOS，提出了Symbian消亡的不同背景和可能的经验教训。

44591062.article_content:
OSes
5
Open, free, and completely ignored: The strange afterlife of Symbian
5
It did get sourced, but nobody cared
Liam Proven
Thu 17 Jul 2025
//
07:27 UTC
The result of the pioneering joint Psion and Nokia smartphone effort is still out there on GitHub.
Smartphones are everywhere. They are entirely commoditized now. Most of them run Android, which uses the Linux kernel. The rest run Apple's iOS, which uses the same XNU kernel as macOS. As we've said before, they're not Unix-like,
they really are Unix™
.
There have been a bunch of others. BlackBerry tried hard with BB10, but even a decade ago,
it was over
. It was based on QNX and Qt, and both of those are doing fine. We
reported last year
that QNX 8 is free to use again. Palm's WebOS
ended up with HP
and now runs in
LG smart TVs
– but it's Linux underneath.
The most radical, though, was probably Symbian.
The Register
covered it at length back in the day, notably the epic
Psion: the Last Computer
feature, followed by the two-part
Symbian, The Secret History
, and
Symbian UI Wars
features.
Built from scratch in the late 1990s in the then-relatively new C++, it evolved into a real-time microkernel OS for handhelds, with the radical
EKA2 microkernel
designed by
Dennis May
and documented in detail in the book
Symbian OS Internals
. There's also
The Symbian OS Architecture Sourcebook
[PDF]. An
official version
of the source code is on GitHub, and
other copies
are out there.
We liked
this
description from
CHERI Project
boffin
David Chisnall
:
The original Symbian kernel was nothing special, but EKA2 (which is the one described in the amazing Symbian Internals book) was a thing of beauty. It had a realtime nano-kernel (does not allocate memory) that could run both an RTOS and a richer application stack. It was a victim of poor timing: the big advantage was the ability to run both the apps and the phone stack on the same core, but it came along as Arm cores became cheap enough that just sticking two in the SoC was cheap enough.
Before Nokia was assimilated and digested by Microsoft, it
open sourced the OS
, and despite some
licensing concerns
, it's still there.
It strikes this vulture as odd that while work continues on some ground-up FOSS OS projects in C++, such as the
Genode OS
, or
Serenity OS
, which we
looked at in 2022
,the more complete Symbian, which shipped on millions of devices and for a while had a thriving third-party application market, languishes ignored.
(Incidentally, the Serenity OS project lead has moved on to the independent
Ladybird browser
, which we
looked at in 2023
. Work on the OS continues, now community-led.)
Google's Android boss suggests ChromeOS could be on borrowed time
GParted: Still the best free partitioner standing – unless you're on a 32-bit box
The price of software freedom is eternal politics
Red Hat sweetens the RHEL deal for biz devs – just don't put it in prod
Symbian's progenitor, Psion EPOC32, predates much of the standardization of C++ – much as BeOS did. We've seen comments that it was not easy to program, but tools such as
P.I.P.S.
made it easier. Nokia
wasted vast effort
on multiple incompatible UIs, which have been blamed for
tearing Symbian apart
, but none of that matters now: adapt some existing FOSS stuff, and forget backwards compatibility. Relatively few of the apps were FOSS, and who needs touchscreen phone apps on a Raspberry Pi anyway? Qt would be ideal – it's a native C++ tool too.
Fans of all manner of 20th century proprietary OSes from AmigaOS to OS/2 bemoan that these never went open source. Some of BeOS made it into
PalmOS Cobalt
but that sank. Palm even
mulled basing an Arm version of PalmOS on Symbian
, but
the deal fell through
.
Some of those OSes have been rebuilt from scratch, including
AmigaOS as AROS
and
BeOS as Haiku
. But they run on Intel. Neither runs natively on Arm, and yet Symbian sits there ignored. Sometimes you can't even give the good stuff away. ®

• **fsflover**：与Symbian的消亡对比，Mobian和postmarketOS等项目却蓬勃发展，引发思考。

补充讨论：
- Symbian的开发难度和工具问题被广泛提及，尤其是内存管理和开发工具的不足。
- 不同开发者对Symbian的体验和看法各异，有的强调其技术优点，有的则批评其生态系统的不足。
- 对现代移动操作系统（如Android和iOS）的批评主要集中在封闭性和应用兼容性问题上。
- 关于Symbian消亡原因的讨论中，硬件发展和市场时机被认为是关键因素。
- 关于现代Linux移动操作系统的成功，如Mobian和postmarketOS，提出了Symbian消亡的不同背景和可能的经验教训。

主要讨论点：不同观点对通过跟随或反向操作金融市场建议（尤其是来自YouTube等平台）的有效性评价

不同观点：
• **gtani的观点**：列举了一系列可以通过YouTube频道获取的全球宏观经济指标，认为通过关注诸如Vix指数、期权流、市场 maker的动态、交易量、债券收益率曲线、信用利差、央行持仓、金属价格、地缘政治动态、能源、货币、商品价差等因素，可以获得市场优势。该评论集中于具体的市场指标，而非直接评价YouTube建议的有效性。

• **GianFabien的观点**：援引了John Paulson和Michael Burry的案例，指出逆势操作（即与大众行为相反）往往能带来巨大成功。特别提到这些投资大佬在2008年金融危机前通过做空CDO获利，并通过电影《大空头》来类比当前可能存在的从众心理现象。该观点强调逆向投资策略的潜在收益。

• **Corgipower12的观点**：通过分析金融YouTube推荐的股票视频并进行回测，发现与这些"金融网红"（finfluencers）建议反向操作，能够获得比标普500更高的年化收益率（+6.8%），但同时伴随更高的波动性。这表明反向操作可能比直接跟随网红建议更有效，但也提示了风险的增加。

• **rfarley04的观点**：质疑反向操作的实际效果，并引用CNBC文章标题暗示"什么都不做"可能比复杂的投资策略更有效，反映了对过度交易或复杂操作的怀疑态度。这一观点挑战了Corgipower12的结论，提出"无为而治"也可能是一种成功的投资策略。

• **nullc的观点**：提到与Hacker News（HN）用户观点反向操作也能够带来可观收益，暗示在某些社区中，主流意见可能存在偏差，进一步支持了逆向投资策略的有效性。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**在于YouTube等平台上的金融建议是否具有实际参考价值。gtani关注具体指标而未评价建议质量，GianFabien和Corgipower12则通过实例和数据支持反向操作，而rfarley04则质疑这种策略是否优于简单持有。
• 讨论中还涉及了**波动性与收益率**的关系，Corgipower12指出反向操作虽能提高收益，但伴随更高波动性，这提示了风险管理的重要性。
• **逆向投资策略**的有效性在多个评论中被提及，尤其是GianFabien和nullc引用的历史案例和社区经验，强调了与大众行为反向操作的潜在收益。

data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论加拿大为何需要建立自己的公共云基础设施，以减少对美国科技巨头的依赖，确保数字主权。目前，加拿大在云计算方面高度依赖美国公司如亚马逊、谷歌、微软和甲骨文，这带来了潜在的风险，尤其是在美国对加拿大采取不友好政策和经济压力的背景下。文章提到，美国通过的《CLOUD法案》允许其政府访问美国公司存储的全球数据，进一步威胁他国数据安全。作者建议，加拿大应由国有企业投资建设公共云，而非仅依赖私营部门，以增强技术自主性并保护本国数字经济利益。

Why Canada needs to build a public cloud
Dependence on US tech giants must end if the country is serious about digital sovereignty

White House
I’ve been writing a lot about
getting off US tech
in an individual capacity and why our governments need to
get serious about digital sovereignty
in recent months. As part of that, the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives asked me to write about what that might look in Canada. I chose to focus on some of the infrastructure that underpins the internet itself, often called the cloud. You can
read it on their website
, but they’ve allowed me to share it with newsletter subscribers too. Enjoy!
Subscribe
During the 2025 election campaign, prime minister Mark Carney made a striking admission about Canada’s dependence on US tech companies. The Canadian government was in the process of choosing a partner for a 25-year cloud computing contract for the federal government. The contract’s length should have set off red flags of its own, but the part that Carney drew attention to was the companies lined up to win it.
The shortlist had been
narrowed down
to four companies: Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Oracle — all US tech giants. At a time when the United States was threatening Canadian sovereignty and waging economic war on the country, the idea of further increasing Canada’s reliance on dominant US tech companies couldn’t fly. Carney promised that if he was reelected, he would review the process. On April 28, the Liberal Party won another minority government.
Carney’s statement was easily overlooked given the flood of other news during the election period, but it was important for a number of reasons. Cloud infrastructure has become essential to the modern world and the digital technologies that power it, but it’s often hidden from view and easy to forget about.
The “cloud” refers to a series of warehouse-sized facilities around the world, filled with tens of thousands of servers and hard drives, that power the internet and many of the services we collectively rely on — our governments included. But those hyperscale data centres are overwhelmingly controlled by those four major tech companies. As the United States becomes a less trustworthy partner, our dependence on them creates a serious vulnerability.
For the past several decades, since the internet’s
privatization
by the US government in 1995, we’ve effectively allowed US companies to dominate the digital economy. When you think about the digital services or devices you rely on today, few if any come from Canadian companies. That not only means our government has less power to protect Canadians’ rights and assert our values online, but also ensures the economic gains are exported to the United States. Its dominant tech companies are a big part of the reason the US economy, and particularly its stock market, performs better than its peers.
Mark Carney caves to Trump and the tech industry
Paris Marx
·
Jun 30
Read full story
Our European allies are also expressing increasing concern about their dependence on the US cloud giants like Microsoft and Google. In recent months, European media reported that Trump could
cut off access
to cloud services offered by US tech companies in Europe to increase pressure on them as part of his trade war. The United States also passed a bill in 2018 called the CLOUD Act that allows the U.S. government to access data stored by U.S. companies, regardless of where in the world it’s held. That’s not an infrastructure any Canadian, and certainly not our government, should be relying on.
As Carney looks to reduce Canada’s dependence on the United States, we can’t ignore the extent of our technological dependence — and the cloud is a great place to start. Carney’s statement during the election suggested he would look to Canadian companies to supply more of the computation and storage needs of the federal government, but he should be far more ambitious.
Instead of simply encouraging the buildout of a private Canadian cloud, the government should invest in the expansion of a public cloud — built and run by a Crown corporation with public financing to serve government needs, but potentially to expand beyond that too. The government already has data centres of its own, but in recent decades it’s more often looked to the private sector to supply more of its computational needs instead of developing in-house capacities as it did with older forms of information technology.

data.author: robin_reala
data.article_summary: noyb组织于2025年7月17日向阿里速卖通、TikTok和微信提交了GDPR投诉，指控它们未遵守GDPR第15条规定的用户数据访问请求，导致欧洲用户无法行使其隐私权，无法了解个人数据如何被处理及公司是否遵守其他GDPR条款。TikTok仅提供了部分无结构数据，阿里速卖通提供的文件损坏，而微信则完全忽略了请求。这些行为使得用户无法验证数据处理的合法性。noyb已在比利时、希腊和荷兰的 data protection authorities (DPAs) 提交投诉，要求这些公司提供完整数据并建议对其进行罚款，罚款最高可达全球收入的4%。

44590617.article_content:
How TikTok, AliExpress & WeChat ignore your GDPR rights
Data Subject Rights
/
17 July 2025
Today,
noyb
has filed GDPR complaints against AliExpress, TikTok and WeChat. All three tech companies have failed to comply with access requests under Article 15 GDPR.  This makes it impossible for European users to exercise their fundamental right to privacy, to find out how their personal data is being processed – and if the companies actually comply with other GDPR provisions, for example regarding data transfers. EU law usually allows users to get a full copy of their data.
Complaint against TikTok (EN)
Complaint against TikTok (EL)
Complaint against AliExpress (EN)
Complaint against AliExpress (FR)
Complaint against WeChat (EN)
Complaint against WeChat (NL)
Chinese Apps are even worse than US Providers.
Most major tech companies have by now implemented some sort of automation tool that allows them to fulfil GDPR access requests on a mass scale, usually via a “download your information” tool. Theoretically, this would make it extremely easy for them to comply with EU law. In reality, however, both TikTok and AliExpress haven’t bothered to give the data subjects access to all of their data as required under Article 15 GDPR. TikTok only provided part of the complainant’s data in an unstructured form that was impossible to understand. AliExpress provided a broken file that could be opened only once. WeChat, on the other hand, just completely ignored the complainant’s request.
Kleanthi Sardeli, data protection lawyer at
noyb
:
“Tech companies love collecting as much data about you as possible – but vehemently refuse to give you full access as required by EU law.”
Unable to verify lawfulness of processing.
Since TikTok and AliExpress provided the complainants with incomplete data, the users sent a series of follow-up questions to give these companies another chance. Instead of supplying the missing data, both companies chose to just repeated the contents of their privacy policy without any individual information. This made it impossible for the complainants to check whether their data has been processed in line with the GDPR.
Follow-up to Chinese data transfer complaints.
The access requests in question were originally filed in preparation for a
series of
noyb
complaints from January 2025
. At the time,
noyb
had taken legal action against TikTok, AliExpress, SHEIN, Temu, WeChat and Xiaomi for unlawful data transfers to China. According to EU law, data transfers outside the EU are only allowed if the destination country doesn’t undermine the protection of data. Given that Chinese laws do not limit access to personal data by the authorities, companies can’t realistically shield EU users’ data from government access. During the proceedings, SHEIN, Temu and Xiaomi provided the complainants with additional information. Meanwhile, TikTok, AliExpress and WeChat continued to violate the GDPR.
Kleanthi Sardeli, data protection lawyer at
noyb
:
“The GDPR makes it clear that companies must give their users specific information about the data they are processing about them. Just because they receive a lot of requests doesn’t mean they can withhold information.”
Complaints filed in three EU countries.
noyb
has therefore filed three complaints with the data protection authorities (DPAs) in Belgium, Greece and the Netherlands. We request that the respective DPAs issue a decision declaring that TikTok, AliExpress and WeChat have violated Article 12 and 15 GDPR. In addition, we request that the companies are ordered to fulfil the complainants’ access requests. Last but not least, we suggest that the DPAs impose an administrative fine to prevent similar violations in the future. Such a fine can reach up to 4% of the global revenue, which can e.g. amount to €147 million
(annual revenue of €3.68 billion)
for AliExpress.

44571692.article_content:
Voxtral
Introducing frontier open source speech understanding models.
Research
Jul 15, 2025
Mistral AI
Voice: the original UI.
Voice was humanity’s first interface—long before writing or typing, it let us share ideas, coordinate work, and build relationships. As digital systems become more capable, voice is returning as our most natural form of human-computer interaction.
Yet today’s systems remain limited—unreliable, proprietary, and too brittle for real-world use. Closing this gap demands tools with exceptional transcription, deep understanding, multilingual fluency, and open, flexible deployment.
We release the Voxtral models to accelerate this future. These state‑of‑the‑art speech understanding models are  available in two sizes—a 24B variant for production-scale applications and a 3B variant for local and edge deployments. Both versions are released under the Apache 2.0 license, and are also available on our
API
. The API routes transcription queries to a transcribe-optimized version of Voxtral Mini (Voxtral Mini Transcribe) that delivers unparalleled cost and latency-efficiency.
Open, affordable, and production-ready speech understanding for everyone.
Until recently, gaining truly usable speech intelligence in production meant choosing between two trade-offs:
Open-source ASR systems with high word error rates and limited semantic understanding
Closed, proprietary APIs that combine strong transcription with language understanding, but at significantly higher cost and with less control over deployment
Voxtral bridges this gap. It offers state-of-the-art accuracy and native semantic understanding in the open, at less than half the price of comparable APIs. This makes high-quality speech intelligence accessible and controllable at scale.
Both Voxtral models go beyond simple transcription with capabilities that include:
Long-form context:
with a 32k token context length, Voxtral handles audios up to 30 minutes for transcription, or 40 minutes for understanding
Built-in Q&A and summarization:
Supports asking questions directly about the audio content or generating structured summaries, without the need to chain separate ASR and language models
Natively multilingual:
Automatic language detection and state-of-the-art performance in the world’s most widely used languages (English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Hindi, German, Dutch, Italian, to name a few), helping teams serve global audiences with a single system
Function-calling straight from voice:
Enables direct triggering of backend functions, workflows, or API calls based on spoken user intents, turning voice interactions into actionable system commands without intermediate parsing steps.
Highly capable at text:
Retains the text understanding capabilities of its language model backbone, Mistral Small 3.1
These capabilities make the Voxtral models ideal for real-world interactions and downstream actions, such as summaries, answers, analysis, and insights. For cost-sensitive use-cases, Voxtral Mini Transcribe outperforms OpenAI Whisper for less than half the price. For premium use cases, Voxtral Small matches the performance of ElevenLabs Scribe, also for less than half the price.
French

0:00
0:15
Benchmarks
Speech Transcription
To assess Voxtral’s transcription capabilities, we evaluate it on a range of English and multilingual benchmarks. For each task, we report the macro-average word error rate (lower is better) across languages. For English, we report a short-form (<30-seconds) and long-form (>30-seconds) average.
Voxtral comprehensively outperforms Whisper large-v3, the current leading open-source Speech Transcription model. It beats GPT-4o mini Transcribe and Gemini 2.5 Flash across all tasks, and achieves state-of-the-art results on English short-form and Mozilla Common Voice, surpassing ElevenLabs Scribe and demonstrating its strong multilingual capabilities.
When evaluated across languages in FLEURS, Voxtral Small outperforms Whisper on every task, achieving state-of-the-art performance in a number of European languages.
Macro-average details:
En short-form: LibriSpeech Clean, LibriSpeech Other, GigaSpeech, VoxPopuli, Switchboard, CHiME-4, SPGISpeech
En long-form: Earnings-21 10-m, Earnings-22 10-m
Mozilla Common Voice 15.1: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Hindi
FLEURS: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Hindi, Arabic
Audio Understanding
Voxtral Small and Mini are capable of answering questions directly from speech, or by providing an audio and a text-based prompt. To evaluate Audio Understanding capabilities, we create speech-synthesized versions of three common Text Understanding tasks. We also evaluate the models on an in-house Audio Understanding (AU) Benchmark, where the model is tasked with answering challenging questions on 40 long-form audio examples. Finally, we assess Speech Translation capabilities on the FLEURS-Translation benchmark

data.title: The companies laying off staff for AI today will regret it in five years
data.author: ekpyrotic
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了企业因人工智能（AI）技术而裁员的现象，并认为这是短视的做法。作者亚历山德拉·埃伯特指出，尽管AI能提高效率、加速流程，但它无法创造新一代产品和服务。创新源于人类，AI只能模仿和回收已有想法，不能引领突破。文章援引麦肯锡的数据表明，注重创新的公司表现更优，并以Blockbuster和Netflix为例说明缺乏前瞻性将导致失败。作者建议企业不应仅通过裁员追求短期利润，而应利用AI给员工更多创新空间，以实现长期成功。最终，善用AI并留住人才的公司将在未来市场中占据主导地位。
data.comments_summary:

44591000.article_content:
Commentary
·
Artificial Intelligence
The companies laying off staff for AI today will regret it in five years
By
Alexandra Ebert
By
Alexandra Ebert
Alexandra Ebert is Chief AI & Data Democratization Officer at Mostly AI.
Alexandra Ebert believes AI can support creative people, but it can’t replace them.
courtesy of mostly ai
You’ve probably seen the headlines. “AI job cuts.” “Automation replacing humans.” Some CEOs are even proud of it.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the next billion-dollar company
could consist of one person
thanks to AI advances. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei thinks AI could
eliminate nearly half of all entry-level white-collar jobs
in five years
Already this year, more than 64,000 people have been laid off across the tech sector, with
Microsoft
and
Intel
leading the charge and AI being a major factor.
People innovate, AI imitates
Not only is this short-sighted, it’s fundamentally bad business. The companies cutting people today in the name of AI will be the ones playing catch-up tomorrow.
There is no doubt that AI is excellent at doing more with less. It speeds up processes, cuts down repetitive work, and buys back time. But AI on its own cannot create the next generation of products and services.
The businesses that win in the long term are the ones that innovate. That create new products. That reimagine how things should work, and find radical breakthroughs that impress their customers in new ways.
The data backs it up.
McKinsey
found that companies with innovation baked into the culture are 3.5 times more likely to outperform their competitors.
And history supports it as well—just ask Blockbuster. Back in the early 2000s, it had strong profits and a large customer base. But what it lacked was the foresight to use its leading position to build the next wave of value.
Netflix
built it instead.
And that kind of creative thinking still only comes from people. Ultimately, it comes down to this: AI doesn’t invent. It recycles. It’s trained on other people’s ideas, imitates patterns, and doesn’t jump the curve.
That’s not a flaw—that’s how AI is designed. As academic Mark Runco puts it: “
AI can only produce artificial creativity
.” It can support creative people, but it can’t replace them.
If your strategy is to lay off the people who could create the next big thing—good luck. You might run a tighter ship, at least in the short term, but don’t be surprised when your product roadmap starts to fall flat.
How AI can really unleash creativity
So, if you’re leading a large business, what should you do instead? Keep hold of your talent. Tell your team to use the extra time they have freed up with AI to innovate. Give your people the headroom to think.
Some of the world’s most successful—and perhaps more importantly profitable—products started as side projects inside
Google
, among them Gmail and AdSense. Not because they were asked for. But because smart people had the space and time to explore.
Imagine if those same people had been made redundant the quarter before. That’s exactly what is happening right now.
Too many leaders are taking the efficiency gains of AI and passing them straight to the bottom line. They’re juicing short-term profits and calling it innovation.
AI limitations
And that’s before you even factor in the risk that many of these so-called “efficiencies” may never materialize. For all the AI hype, humanity doesn’t have the greatest track record when it comes to predicting the future. If the magazines of the 1950s and 1960s were right, we’d be commuting to work with jet packs and cleaning our homes with nuclear-powered hoovers by now.
The same might apply here. Embedding AI into real-world business processes is hard, especially when it comes to sophisticated knowledge work. There are technical limitations, privacy minefields, and the unsolved problem of how to fix or debug AI agents when they go off course.
So, there’s every chance that some of the companies laying off staff today will find themselves quietly rehiring in a few years, once they realize the tech isn’t as capable as they thought.
Taken together, the winners won’t be the companies that cut deepest. They’ll be the ones that keep the right people, give them space, and leverage AI to push their creativity even further.
AI is rewriting the rules of business. What matters now is how you choose to use it. Where one company sees an opportunity to cut headcount, another sees a chance to build something new.
Only one of those will still be leading the market in five years.
The opinions expressed in Fortune.com commentary pieces are solely the views of their authors and do not necessarily reflect the opinions and beliefs of
Fortune
.

, this Fortune 500 boss says taking the focus off real people is a ‘recipe for failure’
AI is replacing human connection as it boosts productivity. Success requires
elevating relationships while embracing the technology

data.title: Upcoming coordinated security fix for all Matrix server implementations
data.author: notpushkin
data.article_summary: Matrix.org基金会宣布将于2025年7月22日UTC 17:00进行一次协调的安全发布，以修复Matrix协议中的两个高严重性漏洞（CVE-2025-49090等）。这些漏洞涉及“状态重置”问题，可能导致意外结果。为解决这些问题，将发布Matrix规范的非周期版本1.16，引入新的房间版本12，并要求升级现有房间。房间管理员应在方便时进行升级，特别是在不信任的联邦中运行的服务器需尽快更新。客户端开发者需注意新的房间ID格式，并调整处理创建者权限的逻辑。基金会已与服务器实现者社区合作，在保密情况下准备此次发布。最终细节将在7月25日公开。感谢社区的支持与理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Matrix平台的现状及其问题，包括内容审核、技术升级和用户体验。

不同观点：
• mystraline认为Matrix平台存在严重的儿童色情/CSAM问题，尤其是在matrix.org的公共聊天室。由于缺乏审核和协议问题，这些非法内容可以长时间传播。他们建议用户不要使用matrix.org的聊天室，关闭图片预加载功能，并推荐使用私人服务器和房间。

• realityfactchex承认公共房间存在垃圾信息问题，但认为私人服务器在信任的朋友之间使用时表现非常好。他们还提到Matrix团队正在进行的状态重置算法升级，并表示如果房间状态变得更加稳定，将是一个很好的改进。

• baby认为当前Matrix的问题不在于去中心化，而在于缺乏一个低成本、支持端到端加密的大型服务器。开放源代码的解决方案可以降低运行服务器的成本。

• willvarfar表示很多人对Matrix是什么以及它的使用体验不太清楚。他询问是否有普通的网页查看器可以在不加入Matrix和使用其应用的情况下查看公共聊天室的内容。

• 42lux则简单地表示IRC过去和现在都是解决方案，暗示IRC可能是一个更好的选择。

补充讨论：
• Matrix平台的公共聊天室审核问题和垃圾信息传播是一个主要争议点，尤其是涉及非法内容时。
• 私人服务器和房间被认为是更安全的选择，但设置和管理这些服务器需要一定的技术能力。
• Matrix团队正在进行的技术升级被一些用户视为积极的改进。
• 对于不熟悉Matrix的用户，存在了解和访问公共聊天室内容的障碍。
• 有些用户认为传统的IRC可能是一个更好的替代方案。

44591820.article_content:
We are happy to launch
The Matrix Conference
on Oct 15-18 in
Strasbourg, France.
Learn more
about it,
buy a
ticket
!
Hi all,
Over the last 6 months a major project has been underway by the Element server team and the Matrix.org Foundation security team to investigate “state resets”: scenarios where Matrix’s state resolution algorithm can give unexpected results.  As part of this work we’ve identified two high severity protocol vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-49090; the other not yet allocated a CVE).
Given the security implications of a federation protocol vulnerability, we’ve shared details under embargo over the last 4 weeks with all known active server implementations, and are now aiming for a coordinated security release across all Matrix server implementations on
Tuesday Jul 22nd 2025 at 17:00 UTC
.  If you run a Matrix server in an untrusted federation (e.g. the public federation), please be prepared to upgrade as soon as the patched versions are available.
These vulnerabilities have been addressed via MSCs which have been shared, reviewed and are in the final comment period (disposition merge) with the Spec Core Team and server implementor community, under embargo.  This will result in an off-cycle Matrix spec release (1.16) introducing a new room version (
12
) to address the vulnerabilities in question, requiring a room upgrade of existing rooms.  Having given server and room admins time to upgrade, we are then planning to un-embargo the MSCs and complement tests on Friday Jul 25th 2025 at 17:00 UTC.
CLARIFICATION, Jul 16 17:30 UTC
: Room admins should plan to upgrade rooms at their convenience, similar to previous security-related room version upgrades (e.g. v1 to v2).  Much like installing an operating system patch, sooner is better, but as these are not Critical Severity vulnerabilities, there is no requirement for room admins to upgrade rooms immediately on Jul 22nd. For instance, the Matrix.org Foundation will likely upgrade its public rooms at some point after Jul 25th (having given server admins a chance to upgrade, and having given any server implementations running late a chance to release).  N.B. Only rooms which include users on potentially malicious servers (e.g. publicly joinable rooms on untrusted federations) are vulnerable.
Important information for client developers:
Client developers should review
MSC4291: “Room IDs as hashes of the create event”
to ensure their clients can accept the new proposed format of room IDs, and no longer expects
content.predecessor.event_id
in
m.room.create
events.
One of the other changes coming in v12 is that room creators will be privileged over other users in the room. Therefore clients which restrict user behaviour based on power level will need to be updated to be aware that room creators effectively have infinite power level. Creators are
not
listed in the users block of the
m.room.power_levels
event, and are instead defined as the
sender
field of the
m.room.create
event, or entries in a new optional
additional_creators
array field in the
content
of the create event. Full details will be released in the MSCs when embargo lifts.
Finally, clients which use
power_level_content_override
when creating rooms MUST NOT assign a power level to the room creator, otherwise the
/createRoom
request will fail.
This has been an exceptionally complicated project to coordinate and its security implications required us to deviate from our usual MSC process and develop the changes under embargo. This and the expedited release of a new stable room version are exceptional choices that are far from ideal, which we’re having to take to keep the ecosystem secure.  To be clear, normal MSC development and process will continue in the open, just as it always has. We’d like to sincerely thank the Matrix server implementor community for their impressive support in preparing the coordinated security releases - both in terms of vital MSC review, and then working together to implement the necessary changes. Matrix’s server heterogeneity has never looked healthier. We’d also like to thank Timo Kösters for helping precipitate the project in the first place.
We’ll follow up with more details next Tuesday (assuming the disclosure timeline doesn’t slip).
Thanks all for your time, patience and understanding while we ship this protocol upgrade (the first coordinated upgrade since
Matrix 1.0
back in 2019!)
Matthew
The Foundation needs you
The Matrix.org Foundation is a non-profit and only relies
on donations to operate. Its core mission is to maintain
the Matrix Specification, but it does much more than that.
It maintains the matrix.org homeserver and hosts several
bridges for free. It fights for our collective rights to
digital privacy and dignity.
Support us

data.title: Archaeologists Discover Tomb of First King of Caracol
data.author: divbzero
data.article_summary: 考古学家Diane和Arlen Chase在1980年代于伯利兹的卡拉科尔（Caracol）发现了古玛雅城市首位统治者Te K'ab Chaak的陵墓。卡拉科尔曾是玛雅历史上重要的政治中心，在公元560至680年间主导尤卡坦半岛南部，直到公元900年被遗弃。Te K'ab Chaak于公元331年登基，其陵墓中出土了陶器、骨管、玉器、马赛克面具、贝壳等陪葬品。陶器上描绘了玛雅统治者、神祇和俘虏的场景。该发现是卡拉科尔四十多年发掘中首个可辨识的统治者陵墓。研究显示，Te K'ab Chaak的陵墓是公元350年左右的三个主要墓葬之一，此时卡拉科尔与中美洲的联系已经非常广泛，甚至受到特奥蒂瓦坎的影响。另两个墓葬也显示出与特奥蒂瓦坎的联系，表明早期玛雅统治者在特奥蒂瓦坎事件前已融入广泛的中美洲交流网络。

44556997.article_content:
Caana, the central architectural complex at Caracol, Belize, uncovered by Diane and Arlen Chase in the 1980s
Archaeologists from the University of Houston working at Caracol in Belize, Central America have uncovered the tomb of Te K’ab Chaak, the first ruler of this ancient Maya city and the founder of its royal dynasty. Now in ruins, this metropolis was a major political player in Maya history, dominating the southern part of the Yucatan Peninsula from 560 through 680 AD before its abandonment by 900 AD.
The discovery is the first identifiable ruler’s tomb found in over four decades of work in Caracol, the largest Maya archaeological site in Belize and in the Maya lowlands.
Te K’ab Chaak, who acceded to the throne in 331 AD, was interred at the base of a royal family shrine with eleven pottery vessels, carved bone tubes, jadeite jewelry, a mosaic jadeite mask, Pacific spondylus shells, and other perishable materials. Pottery vessels in the chamber included a scene of a Maya ruler holding a spear and receiving offerings from supplicants in the form of deities. Another vessel portrays the image of Ek Chuah, Maya god of traders, surrounded by offerings. Four of the pottery vessels portray bound captives (similar vessels also appeared in two related burials). Two vessels supported lids with modeled handles of coatimundi (pisote) heads. The coatimundi, or tz’uutz’ in Maya, was used by subsequent Caracol rulers as part of their names.
Archaeologist Diane Chase in the recently excavated tomb
Maya pottery basal flange bowl with a coatimundi head
Four jadeite tubular beads showing live and dead spider monkeys
Archaeologists Arlen and Diane Chase will soon celebrate their 50th wedding anniversary.
A team led by husband and wife collaborators Arlen F. Chase and Diane Z. Chase of the University of Houston has been excavating at Caracol for more than 40 years; this field season was carried out in concert with Belize’s Institute of Archaeology and was supported by the Alphawood Foundation, the University of Houston, the Geraldine and Emory Ford Foundation, and the KHR Family Fund.
The Chases estimate that at the time of his burial the ruler was of advanced age and approximately 5’7” in height. He had no remaining teeth.
Their investigations at Caracol’s Northeast Acropolis show that Te K’ab Chaak’s tomb was the first of three major burials dating to about 350 AD, a time of early contact with the central Mexican city of Teotihuacan, some 1200 kilometers distant. By 300 AD, Teotihuacan was a huge city that traded throughout Central America.
“One question that has perplexed Maya archaeologists since the 1960s is whether a new political order was introduced to the Maya area by Mexicans from Teotihuacan,” said Diane Z. Chase, archaeologist and senior vice president for academic affairs and Provost at the University of Houston.
“Maya carved stone monuments, hieroglyphic dates, iconography, and archaeological data all suggest that widespread pan-Mesoamerican connections occurred after an event in 378 AD referred to as ‘entrada,’” said Diane Chase.
“Whether this event represented actual Teotihuacanos in the Maya area or Maya using central Mexican symbols is still debated. The Caracol archaeological data suggests that the situation was far more complicated,” she said.
A cremation placed in the center of Caracol’s Northeast Acropolis plaza, recovered in 2010 and placed after Te K’aab Chaak’s burial has been dated to AD 350 by radiocarbon analysis and included artifacts from central Mexico. It contained the remains of three individuals, as well as two large knives, six atlatl points, and fifteen pristine blades of green obsidian from Pachuca, Mexico (north of Teotihuacan); several pottery vessels also likely came from central Mexico. Additionally, a carved atlatl projectile tip, atypical for the Maya but typical for a Teotihuacan warrior, was included in the cremation.
The cremation itself and its placement in the center of a residential plaza are also more typical practices for a high-status Teotihuacano and do not accord with standard Maya burial practices. Based on other ceramics in this cremation, the main individual was likely a Caracol royal family member that had adopted central Mexican ritual practices. This individual may even have served as a royal Maya envoy who had lived at Teotihuacan and returned to Caracol.
A third burial — the tomb of a woman, also covered with hematite and containing four pottery vessels, a spondylus bead necklace, mirror fragments, and two Pacific spondylus shells — was recovered in the northern building of the same residential group in 2009 and is similarly dated.
The three burials interred in the Caracol Northeast Acropolis all cluster at AD 350, at least a generation before the previously recognized Teotihuacan presence in the Maya area. They demonstrate that early Maya rulers were fully enmeshed in Mesoamerican-wide contacts prior to the Teotihuacan entrada recorded on Maya monument[s].

data.article_summary: 该文章列出了多个流媒体房间的链接，包括EL11（Geosolutions）、SA01、SA02、CA01（TomTom）、PA01（Quarticle），以及位于波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那莫斯塔尔的联系信息和电子邮件地址（info-europe@foss4g.org）。同时提到网站使用cookies，继续浏览即表示同意其使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FOSS4G（Free and Open Source Software for Geospatial）年度会议的讨论内容、参会体验以及会议视频资源的获取。

不同观点：
• [N_Lens] 对会议中关于AI控制机器人利用地理空间数据的讨论感兴趣，尤其是当前大量投资涌入的背景下。他认为如果人工智能、边缘计算和开放地理空间标准（FOSS4G的核心）继续融合发展，可能会出现大量的机器人代理在物理空间中活动。他举例说明这些机器人可能类似于“非常智能的送货无人机”，而非电影中的“终结者”形象。

• [admaiora] 分享了参加FOSS4G会议的个人经验，认为无论是否直接从事地理空间领域工作，参加会议都会有收获。他特别提到，即使只是网页开发者，了解一些如Leaflet等地理工具也是有价值的。

• [qwertox] 关注会议视频的获取，询问会议直播录像何时以及在哪里可以观看。

• [dabber21] 对所有直播流同时开始的情况表示惊讶，可能在观看体验上遇到了一些不便。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的趋势包括大语言模型（LLMs）在空间推理方面的进步、边缘计算使得移动机器人的实时处理成为可能，以及开放地理空间标准在未来机器人广泛应用中的重要性。
• [N_Lens] 提到了当前技术趋势的融合可能带来的未来场景，引发对未来技术发展和应用的想象和讨论。

争议焦点：
• 目前没有明显的争议，但[N_Lens] 对AI控制机器人利用地理空间数据的未来设想可能引发不同的看法，特别是关于技术发展方向和潜在影响的乐观或悲观预期。

data.title: Retro gaming YouTuber Once Were Nerd sued and raided by the Italian government
data.author: BallsInIt
data.article_summary: 意大利YouTuber Once Were Nerd因展示和评测基于Android的游戏掌机而遭到警方调查，这些设备支持模拟老式游戏机，并预装了大量未经授权的游戏ROM。意大利财政卫队（Guardia di Finanza）没收了他超过30台掌机，并要求他提供与设备制造商的通信记录。尽管模拟软件本身不违法，但这些掌机预装的盗版游戏可能违反了意大利版权法第171条，最高可判三年监禁。设备制造商多在中国，利用法律灰色地带销售产品。此事件可能导致该YouTuber面临刑事指控并关闭频道。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意大利根据版权法对YouTube创作者Once Were Nerd展开调查并可能判刑，引发了对版权执法过度、法律公平性以及更广泛的知识产权讨论的争议。

不同观点：
• **观点一：执法过度，案件无实际受害者**  
  [user_7832], [Tade0], [marcofiset]等认为，此案中的执法行为过于严苛，尤其是针对一个并未造成实际损害的“无受害者犯罪”。他们质疑，对一个20年历史的游戏机和游戏的版权保护是否需要如此严厉的刑法，且意大利的版权执法历史一向严格。参与讨论者认为，此类案件不应动用刑事手段，尤其不应涉及监禁。

• **观点二：版权保护应被认真对待，尤其是商业侵权**  
  [Chronoyes]认为，商业层面上的版权侵权行为不应被轻视。他指出，许多YouTube大频道在公开评测中使用盗版游戏，并与个人下载ROM的行为区分开来。他特别提到，本案中的创作者不仅评测设备，还涉嫌销售盗版设备，这种行为值得严肃处理。

• **观点三：法律不公，大公司与个人之间的执法不平等**  
  [elric], [awongh], [jmyeet]等人指出，现行法律对个人和小型创作者过于严苛，而对大公司（如使用LLM技术的公司）则相对宽松。他们认为，现行版权法和执法存在双重标准，尤其是大公司（如AI公司）能够规避法律责任，而个人创作者却可能因较轻微的违规行为面临严重的法律后果。

• **观点四：版权法的适用和自由表达的冲突**  
  [basfo], [xg15]等认为，购买和展示合法销售的产品（如中国产游戏机）属于自由表达的权利范畴。将此类行为定为犯罪是对自由表达的侵犯。他们质疑，如果要打击盗版，应该从源头上阻止这些设备进入市场，而非惩罚个人创作者。

补充讨论：
• **LLM技术与版权法的潜在冲突**  
  [awongh], [bgwalter]等人提到，LLM（如ChatGPT）在训练过程中使用受版权保护的材料，但这些技术公司却未受到类似严厉的执法，显示出现行法律在技术发展面前的滞后性和不公。

• **意大利执法机构的过度军事化**  
  [Tade0]特别提到，意大利使用 Guardia di Finanza（财政卫队）这种高度军事化的执法部门处理此类案件，显得过于夸张，常规警察足以应对。

• **对公司高管和个人执法的双重标准**  
  [amelius]提出，在隐私侵犯等案件中，公司高管并未受到类似的刑事处罚，显示出执法中的双重标准问题。

争议焦点：  
此次执法是否过度，以及现行版权法是否公平合理，尤其是在个人创作者与大公司之间存在明显的法律适用不公的情况下，是否需要进行版权法的改革。

There are countless Android-powered gaming handhelds, but they go beyond the usual slate of Android games by offering console emulation support. The problem is the
game ROMs
on these devices, which are not entirely legal. Italian YouTuber Once Were Nerd is learning how seriously some rightsholders are taking game piracy after agents from the country's Guardia di Finanza showed up to confiscate his consoles. He now says the investigation could lead to criminal charges and the end of his channel.
Once Were Nerd has produced YouTube content covering a plethora of gaming topics, including Android-based handheld game machines from the likes of Powkiddy and TrimUI. These devices usually run an older version of Android that has been heavily modified for gaming, featuring built-in emulation support for retro consoles like SNES, Nintendo 64, PlayStation Portable, GameCube, and more. They've become quite popular as the cost of mobile hardware has come down, making it possible to buy what is essentially an updated PSP or Game Boy Advance for $100 or less.
Recently, Once Were Nerd attracted the attention of Italy's Ministry of Economy and Finance, which is tasked with policing copyright in the country. In the video first spotted by
Android Authority
(which has an AI-generated English language track), the YouTuber explains that Guardia di Finanza appeared at his door in April with a search warrant.
Once Were Nerd explains his legal woes.
Agents accused the creator of promoting pirated copyrighted materials stemming from his coverage of Anbernic handheld game consoles. While emulation software is not illegal, a surprising number of these devices ship chock-full of pre-loaded ROMs—the channel showed multiple Sony and Nintendo games running on the device. Once Were Nerd is far from the only channel posting about these devices, though.
Officials seized more than 30 handheld consoles and demanded copies of Once Were Nerd's correspondence with the companies making these devices. Once Were Nerd says he has cooperated fully with investigators and contends that he has done nothing wrong.
Legal gray area
The firms making these handhelds all operate out of China, which is beyond the reach of Western copyright law. They still sell the devices internationally, sticking to vague language about the inclusion of game ROMs. For example, Anbernic offers bundles with microSD cards marked as "compatible 7000+ games." That makes this approach to revisiting retro games a legal gray area at the very least. Authorities believe Once Were Nerd's activities may still run afoul of Article 171 in Italy's copyright law, which allows for up to three years imprisonment for violations.
It is unclear who made the original complaint against the channel. Once Were Nerd has seen documents that cite copyrighted material from Nintendo and Sony, but Guardia di Finanza doesn't need to reveal that detail until the preliminary investigation is finished, and cases can be brought by the agency itself. Our money is on Nintendo, which is
particularly litigious
when it comes to defending its intellectual property. When the investigation is complete, the government will either file charges or dismiss the case. Current law also gives officials the power to shut down the Once Were Nerd channel while the investigation is ongoing.
Italy has a history of heavy-handed copyright enforcement—the country's Internet regulator recently
demanded that Google poison DNS
to block illegal streams of soccer. So it's not hard to believe investigators would pursue a case against someone who posts videos featuring pirated games on YouTube.

data.title: ESA’s Moonlight programme: Pioneering the path for lunar exploration (2024)
data.author: nullhole
data.article_summary:
ESA的Moonlight计划旨在建立欧洲首个专用于月球电信和导航服务的卫星 constellation，以支持未来400多项月球任务。该计划将实现如卫星导航、视频会议和文件共享等服务在月球上的无缝使用。Moonlight将由五颗卫星组成，其中一颗用于高数据率通信，四颗用于导航，通过三个地面站与地球连接，覆盖范围达40万公里。该项目优先覆盖月球南极，该地区因地形优势适合未来操作。

Moonlight的第一步是2026年发射的Lunar Pathfinder卫星，作为后续完整星座的先导。随后，Moonlight服务将逐步部署，计划在2028年底开始初步运行，2030年全面运行。ESA正与NASA和JAXA合作制定LunaNet标准，以确保兼容性，并计划在2029年进行首次月球导航互操作性测试。此外，ESA还在考虑未来的火星通信和导航基础设施（MARCONI），利用Moonlight的经验和技术。Moonlight的启动仪式在米兰国际宇航大会上举行，标志着欧洲在支持月球商业市场和国际合作方面迈出了关键一步。

不同观点：

• [优先事项的质疑] jcfrei对当前优先事项提出质疑，认为ESA在考虑月球连接性之前，应先解决地球上的通信问题，尤其是推动IRIS2项目以确保欧洲拥有自主的卫星通信能力。同时提到IRIS2项目预算仍未完全批准，计划2029年才发射，存在一定的急迫性和担忧。

• [文学关联] delijati提到了Daniel Suarez的《Delta-V》或《Critical Mass》这本书，可能是通过科幻文学的角度来看待当前的月球探索项目，但未提出具体的技术或项目评价。

• [支持与赞赏] CharlesXY对ESA主导这一项目表示赞赏和惊喜，认为ESA在推动如此 ambitious 的项目方面表现出色，并对欧洲在太空探索中的领导地位表示认可。

• [长远影响] BigChemical强调了Moonlight项目的重要性，认为它可能成为关键的基础设施项目，使月球探索转变为长期可持续的开发，重点在于让月球变得“可用”而非仅仅插旗宣示主权。

• 争议的焦点之一是当前项目的优先级问题，特别是jcfrei提出的对IRIS2项目进展缓慢的担忧，与ESA在月球项目上的投入形成对比。
• 另一个讨论点是月球导航和通信系统的潜在长远影响，BigChemical特别指出这将改变月球探索的性质，使其从短期任务转变为长期基础设施建设。

44560390.article_content:
ESA
/
Applications
/
Connectivity and Secure Communications
Imagine a near future where services such as satellite navigation, video conferencing, and file sharing are as seamless on the Moon as they are on Earth.
That’s the vision of ESA’s Moonlight programme, which aims to establish Europe’s first-ever dedicated satellite constellation for telecommunication and navigation services for the Moon. With over 400 planned lunar missions by space agencies and private companies in the next two decades, this programme marks a significant step towards sustainable lunar exploration and the development of a lunar economy.
The Moonlight Lunar Communications and Navigation Services (LCNS) programme is a partnership project between ESA and an industry consortium led by space systems developer Telespazio, with support from the UK and Italian Space Agencies. The programme will enable precise, autonomous landings and surface mobility, while facilitating high-speed, low-latency communication and data transfer between Earth and the Moon. This infrastructure is essential for humanity's return to and long-term presence on the Moon, while enhancing efficiency and significantly reducing operational and user costs.
A satellite constellation for lunar navigation and connectivity
Moonlight will be a constellation of five lunar satellites (one for high data rate communications and four for navigation), launched into space and carried by space tug from Earth’s orbit to the Moon’s. The constellation will connect to Earth via three dedicated ground stations, creating a data network spanning up to 400 000 km.
The Moonlight LCNS satellites will be strategically positioned to prioritise coverage of the lunar south pole, an area suitable for future operations due to its advantageous terrain. This includes elevated areas or "peaks of eternal light" – ideal for solar power – and "craters of eternal darkness" containing polar ice – a potential source of water, oxygen and rocket fuel.
The first step in this ambitious programme is the Lunar Pathfinder, a communications relay satellite manufactured by Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd (SSTL) and set to begin operations in 2026. This pioneering spacecraft will serve as a precursor to the full LCNS constellation, providing commercial data relay services and testing existing Earth-orbiting navigation satellites for lunar use. Following the Lunar Pathfinder, Moonlight services will be gradually deployed, with initial operations by the end of 2028 and full operations by 2030.
Collaboration and future plans
ESA is working closely with NASA and JAXA on LunaNet, a new framework for lunar communication and navigation standards. LunaNet ensures compatibility with future lunar infrastructures and technologies, allowing our global customer base to benefit from the services for their own missions or deploy complementary technologies to enhance the network. Moonlight will comply with LunaNet’s standards and undergo the first-ever lunar navigation interoperability tests, scheduled for 2029.
In addition to other programmes, Moonlight will contribute to a multi-planetary future by supporting the testing of instruments and facilities in lunar conditions, helping us better understand their performance in environments other than Earth. Looking further ahead, ESA is taking early steps towards a Mars Communication and Navigation Infrastructure (MARCONI), leveraging the technologies and experiences gained from the Moonlight programme.
[From top-bottom, left-right] Alexander Gerst, ESA astronaut; Daniel Neuenschwander, ESA Director of Human and Robotic Exploration; Javier Benedicto, ESA Director of Navigation; Gabriele Pieralli, Telespazio Chief Executive Officer; Laurent Jaffart, ESA Director of Connectivity and Secure Communications
ESA officially commenced the Moonlight programme with a contract signing ceremony at the International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Milan. The ceremony was attended by Laurent Jaffart, ESA Director of Connectivity and Secure Communications; Javier Benedicto, ESA Director of Navigation; Daniel Neuenschwander, ESA Director of Human and Robotic Exploration; and Gabriele Pieralli, Chief Executive Officer of Telespazio.
“ESA is taking the crucial step in supporting the future commercial lunar market, as well as ongoing and future lunar missions. We are extremely proud to be working with industry and Member States to ensure that our technological capabilities can support and foster cooperation on the Moon with our international partners,” said Josef Aschbacher, ESA Director General.
"This year saw the first commercial soft landing on the moon, and we expect there to be hundreds of new lunar missions launching over the next decade alone. With these missions will come increased demand for communications and navigation services which can be provided by commercial entities,” said Dr Paul Bate, Chief Executive of the UK Space Agency. “The growth of a commercial lunar economy can bring real benefits

data.title: The AI bubble today is bigger than the IT bubble in the 1990s
data.author: akyuu
data.article_summary: 本文由Apollo首席经济学家Torsten Sløk于2025年7月16日撰写，指出当前的AI泡沫比1990年代的IT泡沫更大。文章比较了标普500指数中市值前十的公司，发现如今这些公司的估值过高问题比1990年代更为严重。文章提醒，所述内容仅为截至2025年7月的观点，可能会随时变化，不构成投资建议，投资者应自行调查并咨询专业顾问。同时，Apollo不对这些信息的准确性和完整性做任何保证，也不承担任何责任。注意，文中包含的前瞻性陈述可能与实际结果不同。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI领域的现状、泡沫可能性及其未来发展

不同观点：
• JCM9：认为当前的AI热潮与.com泡沫类似，技术本身有价值，但许多相关企业的商业模式不可持续。许多AI公司将失败或被出售，技术本身会变得普遍但不会成为独立的盈利中心。
• sigmoid10：当人们讨论泡沫而利率下降时是投资的好时机。当前的AI热潮可能会继续，因为现金依然廉价，但这并不意味着可以 indefinitely 持续。
• lucidone：认为AI在日常工作中很有用，但并没有显著改变工作流程，只是取代了部分工具如Stackoverflow。
• EZ-E：承认AI有明确的应用场景，但反对在每个产品或服务中强行加入不合适的AI功能，认为这是泡沫所在。
• vincefutr23：指出任何结论都可以找到支持的图表数据，暗示对单个数据点不应过度解读。
• Havoc：认为大部分AI生态系统会像pets.com一样崩溃，但底层技术是有效的，少数公司会变得更强。
• HPsquared：认为整体经济泡沫化，AI热潮与此有关。
• itomato：提出早期优势在于获取一级ISP访问，而现在只是现金和数据中心容量问题。
• lvl155：认为当前情况与.com泡沫不同，市场没有出现类似的大规模投机行为。
• torginus：投资者可能对AI未来的不同发展路径有计划，无论AI是否变得超智能或仅限于现有水平，Nvidia可能在“卖铲子”中占据垄断地位。
• khurs：引用Gartner的HypeCycle，认为当前AI处于炒作周期中。
• rayiner：不认为AI被高估，认为LLM确实具有革命性，能完成如写论文等任务。
• orangebread：提出存在meta-bubble和normie-bubble，大公司追逐超智能，而普通人在过度使用AI。
• roflcopter69：不反对对AI的投资，但反感虚假承诺，指出AI在实际应用中仍存在不足。
• dcchambers：认为AI泡沫破裂时会比.com泡沫更严重，因为当前许多公司在没有产品的情况下估值过高。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否存在泡沫，以及当前的热潮是否可持续。部分评论者认为AI技术本身有价值，但商业模式或市场行为存在问题，而另一些人则认为AI过度炒作且存在虚假承诺。
• 讨论中也涉及对Nvidia等公司在AI领域垄断地位的看法，以及对AI在实际应用中的局限性和潜力的不同见解。

data.title: N8n vs. node-red, which to use for AI workloads
data.author: daniel-payne
data.article_summary:
本文对比了n8n和Node-RED两种工具，帮助用户根据需求选择适合的平台。主要观点如下：

- **n8n**：适合处理公共云服务数据，集成AI能力强，尤其是与LangGraph和LangSmith结合使用，但缺乏内置的用户界面（UI）进行数据可视化，通常需结合ObservableHQ实现。
  
- **Node-RED**：适合处理私有数据源，尤其是文件和传感器数据，拥有出色的可视化工具Dashboard 2。然而，在处理需要大量AI计算的任务时，Node-RED表现不足，通常需结合FlowiseAI使用。

此外，文章强调了AI伦理问题，指出由于LLM（大语言模型）的非确定性，记录和分析决策过程至关重要。

总结：n8n适合云服务和AI任务，Node-RED则在私有数据和可视化上表现更优，用户可根据具体需求选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Self-hosted（自托管）与云服务的比较

不同观点：
• adastra22认为，自托管和云服务是更大的区别因素。自托管意味着用户自己管理基础设施，拥有更高的控制权和隐私，但同时也增加了维护的复杂性和成本。
• 一部分评论者支持云服务，认为其优势在于便捷性、扩展性和由服务提供商提供的技术支持。这些评论者强调，云服务可以降低运营成本，并快速响应业务需求。
• 另一部分评论者则支持自托管方案，指出自托管可以避免供应商锁定，同时对数据有更高的控制权，特别适用于对数据隐私和安全有较高要求的情况。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于控制权和便捷性之间的权衡。支持自托管的评论者认为安全性和隐私更为重要，而支持云服务的评论者则强调运营效率和成本效益。
• 有评论者提到混合方案的可能性，即结合自托管和云服务的优点，根据具体需求选择合适的解决方案。
• 具体例子包括：自托管在合规性要求较高的行业（如金融和医疗）中更为常见，而云服务则在初创企业和快速发展的科技公司中受到青睐。

Try both, but my personal opinion is:
n8n
if you are using
public
cloud services for your data. But you will need to use something else if you want to visualize your information, e.g.
ObservableHQ
.
node-red
if you are using
private
sources, especially file based data or sensor data. But you will need to use something else for AI intensive workloads, e.g.
FlowiseAI
.
Reasoning
There are only basically two purposes when creating commercial computer systems;
Improve decision making; by turning data into information.
and
Reduce Boredom; by spiking dopamine or releasing serotonin.
There is a third, produce regulatory data. But that’s very boring and you don’t want to read about that.
Decision Making
I don’t know very much about reducing boredom, so I will concentrate on how these two tools can improving decision making.
Both products are focused on turning data into information, and sometimes that information is a trigger for another system to do something. They both excel at this task, however each lack one main component that is needed for effective transformations.
n8n is missing a UI
In my experience you can’t just create a computer system and leave it to run. That way lies disaster, all systems need “baby sitting”. Even in transforming data, we need to see intermediate steps, progress information and summaries of results.
node-red
has
Dashboard 2
, an excellent visualization library built around vueifity and chartJS.
n8n
is missing this, so I use
ObservableHQ
as my go-to visualization solution, but it can be a bit of a kludge accessing live logs.
node-red is missing Antigenic AI
These days we need to use LLMs to transform data, as well as extracting insights.
node-red
does have some LLM nodes, but it is missing integration with
LangGraph
, the main tool that is used to create Antigenic workflows.
n8n
is fully integrated into this landscape, and has excellent nodes for Antigenic AI.
node-red
is missing this, so I use
Flowise AI
as my platform for doing all things Antigenic. But I use
node-red
to prepare my data and put it into storage systems that
Flowise
can use.
node-red
is good at ingesting data into relational databases, creating vectors (with it’s basic LLM nodes) for storage, and also processing data ready for ingestion into graph data-stores. The
Dashboard 2
visualization is very important in ensuring things don’t go wrong; bad data in = bad information out.
AI Ethics
If you are new to AI and just starting out, AI ethics wont mean much, but it is going to be very important once you start building commercial systems.
The issue with AI is that it is
LLMs are non-deterministic; that is each time you run something you might get a different answer.
When you make decisions based on AI, you should always record the data & process that lead to the decision, document and log everything, especially in production.
As time goes by you will need to analyse all the bad decisions your system has made, so that you can improve future performance. You might also have to compensate prior consumers if they are effected by bad decisions.
Both
n8n
and
node-red
have good tools to record to persistent storage. However self-hosted
n8n
has the advantage here, as it has integration with
LangSmith
, a tool for monitoring AI.

44592006.article_summary:
本文对比了n8n和Node-RED两种工具，帮助用户根据需求选择适合的平台。主要观点如下：

- **n8n**：适合处理公共云服务数据，集成AI能力强，尤其是与LangGraph和LangSmith结合使用，但缺乏内置的用户界面（UI）进行数据可视化，通常需结合ObservableHQ实现。
  
- **Node-RED**：适合处理私有数据源，尤其是文件和传感器数据，拥有出色的可视化工具Dashboard 2。然而，在处理需要大量AI计算的任务时，Node-RED表现不足，通常需结合FlowiseAI使用。

此外，文章强调了AI伦理问题，指出由于LLM（大语言模型）的非确定性，记录和分析决策过程至关重要。

总结：n8n适合云服务和AI任务，Node-RED则在私有数据和可视化上表现更优，用户可根据具体需求选择。
44592006.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Self-hosted（自托管）与云服务的比较

不同观点：
• adastra22认为，自托管和云服务是更大的区别因素。自托管意味着用户自己管理基础设施，拥有更高的控制权和隐私，但同时也增加了维护的复杂性和成本。
• 一部分评论者支持云服务，认为其优势在于便捷性、扩展性和由服务提供商提供的技术支持。这些评论者强调，云服务可以降低运营成本，并快速响应业务需求。
• 另一部分评论者则支持自托管方案，指出自托管可以避免供应商锁定，同时对数据有更高的控制权，特别适用于对数据隐私和安全有较高要求的情况。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于控制权和便捷性之间的权衡。支持自托管的评论者认为安全性和隐私更为重要，而支持云服务的评论者则强调运营效率和成本效益。
• 有评论者提到混合方案的可能性，即结合自托管和云服务的优点，根据具体需求选择合适的解决方案。
• 具体例子包括：自托管在合规性要求较高的行业（如金融和医疗）中更为常见，而云服务则在初创企业和快速发展的科技公司中受到青睐。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于编程语言Ada的历史、应用及其与其他语言（如Rust）的对比

不同观点：
• [danbruc] 指出图表的y轴未从零开始，使得差异看起来比实际大。这是一个关于数据可视化准确性的技术性评论，不直接涉及Ada语言本身。

• [tombert] 认为Ada是一种设计精良的语言，本不应该失败，并认为它应该在90年代和2000年代成为许多桌面应用程序的标准。该评论反映了对Ada语言潜力的肯定和对其实际应用未达预期的遗憾。

• [rustcleaner] 质疑Mozilla在已经有Ada/SPARK的情况下为何还要创造Rust语言，暗示Rust可能是对已有解决方案的重复发明，带有对Rust存在必要性的怀疑态度。

• [whartung] 表示失望，原本期待看到关于用Ada编写zip编码器的具体讨论，包括Ada语言在实际编程任务中的优劣。这反映了对评论内容与预期不符的不满，并希望获得更多关于Ada实际应用的详细信息。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Ada语言的历史失败原因及其与新兴语言如Rust的关系。部分评论者对Ada未能广泛应用感到不解和遗憾。

• 另一个值得注意的点是[whartung]对具体技术细节和案例的期待，显示出读者对实际编程实例和语言应用场景的兴趣。

• 评论中还隐含了对不同编程语言竞争和选择的讨论，特别是对新兴语言如Rust和传统语言如Ada之间选择的理由和动机。

data.author: whobre
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对早期计算领域人物和设备的讨论

不同观点：
• BruceEel提供了Gary Kildall的回忆录《Computer Connections》的链接，引导读者查阅相关资料，以深入了解Kildall对计算机历史的贡献。
• Pieterk将讨论引向Sinclair C5车辆，提供了一个维基百科链接，展示了对Sinclair其他车辆的兴趣，将讨论从计算机领域扩展到更广泛的科技产品。
• EconomistFar比较了两位对早期计算有贡献的人物，一位是草根出身的 garage entrepreneur，另一位是体制内的革新者，强调了创新路径和影响力的多样性。

补充讨论：
• Twothreeone的评论带有调侃性质，提到英国幽默在Hacker News（HN）上的体现，虽然与主要讨论主题无直接关系，但增添了对话的趣味性。
• Comrade1234的评论似乎期待一个与历史人物Barbarossa（即神圣罗马帝国皇帝 Frederick I）相关的讨论，与计算机主题无直接关联，显示出对不同话题的期望。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中没有明显的争议，但pieterk将话题转向了Sinclair C5，偏离了Gary Kildall和计算机历史的最初主题，显示出讨论方向的分歧。

总的来说，评论中既有对早期计算贡献者的关注，也有对其他科技产品的兴趣，同时夹杂了一些幽默和题外话。

data.title: Gmail/Google starts disabling features unless you agree to data processing
data.author: diggan
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Workspace 数据处理和功能之间的关系，以及用户对数据使用和收费的争议

不同观点：
• doctaj 认为，Google 并非故意扣留功能，而是因为没有数据就无法提供某些功能，例如日历中的航班信息需要访问电子邮件数据。
• jsnell 指出，Google 并没有不受限制地使用数据，数据使用范围已经明确限定在 Workspace 应用内。他还提到，相关设置已经存在多年，并根据各地法律/法规在不同国家默认开启或关闭。
• kotaKat 抱怨，即使关闭了所有相关功能，Google 仍然会因“AI”功能提高 Workspace 计划的价格，认为这是不合理的收费。
• xnx 质疑那些抱怨新功能的人，认为提供可选择关闭新功能的选项反而招致抱怨，有些不合逻辑。
• bbstats 简单表示，描述中的数据只是 Google 请求访问的数据，并没有实质性问题。
• pavel_lishin 提到，早期的一个功能（邮件到日历自动化）一直有问题，因此他总是关闭该功能。
• jstummbillig 认为，如果不允许数据处理，那么相关功能不工作是可以理解的。
• knorker 强调，Google 是在请求数据处理权限以提供这些功能，如果不允许，这些功能就不应该存在。
• antisol 虽然认为情况不理想，但质疑在 2025 年仍然使用 Gmail 却不希望数据被收集的用户的选择。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于用户是否应该为了使用某些功能而必须允许 Google 处理其数据，以及 Google 是否在通过这些功能和数据使用上进行不合理的收费。
• 不同用户对功能和数据使用的优先级有不同的看法，一些用户更关注功能的可控性，而另一些用户则对数据隐私和费用增加表示不满。
• 讨论中还提到了法律和地域差异对功能默认设置的影响，以及用户对 AI 功能和自动化工具的复杂感受。

data.title: NINA: Rebuilding the original AIM, AOL Desktop, Yahoo and ICQ platforms
data.author: ecliptik
data.article_summary: 这篇文章宣布了一个项目，旨在重现昔日的即时通讯平台，如AOL Instant Messenger (AIM)、ICQ、Yahoo Messenger和经典AOL客户端。项目团队正在努力尽可能接近原版重建这些服务，并记录整个过程。目前，AIM和ICQ已可自由使用，其中ICQ仍在开发中；AOL 4.0和5.0的支持处于alpha阶段，仅对支持者开放；Yahoo Messenger已公开可用并与Escargot网络互通。文章还提到Q-Link（Commodore 64上的AOL前身）以及提供社交平台和社区支持，包括Discord、Reddit、论坛和Wiki。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对即时通讯软件（如Jabber、ICQ、AIM等）过去和现在的技术复兴、怀旧情感及其实用性的讨论。

不同观点：
• [怀旧与复兴支持者] lukaslalinsky怀念Jabber短暂兴盛的时代，认为那段时间的跨平台互通体验非常好，尽管很快结束。同时，bobsmith432提到现在有开发者在逆向工程Skype，并分享相关项目链接。
• [开源与闭源争议] fishgoesblub批评某些复兴项目未开源，并提到目前有开源的AIM服务器项目。marcodiego也质疑为何不贡献于现有的自由开源软件（FLOSS）实现，而是重新构建旧平台。
• [怀旧但怀疑实用性] iforgotpassword认为这些复兴项目虽然酷，但有点“毫无意义”，因为过去的体验无法完全重现，怀旧情绪更适合偶尔回忆。benguild同样认为，曾经的用户群体无法重现，体验无法回到过去。
• [技术与安全考虑] musicale关注现代安全威胁下的加密问题，询问在服务器系统中如何实现安全通信。
• [特定功能重要性] bastardoperator认为AOL的“个人文件柜”功能至关重要，它的消失意味着AOL的彻底消亡。
• [其他类比与现代替代] lvturner指出ICQ实际上仍在通过腾讯QQ延续。ljlolel提到Hangout.fm类似于AOL聊天室，并带有音乐功能。whalesalad则提到Adium和Pidgin作为现代的多协议聊天客户端。

补充讨论：
• [个人情感与文化影响] 多个用户（如acheron、icedchai、pjmlp）表达了对AIM等老一代即时通讯软件的怀旧情绪，部分用户认为这些软件在他们的互联网历史中占据重要位置。
• [创建新互联网] nickdothutton提出了一种更积极的观点，鼓励用户去创造他们想要的互联网，而不是仅仅怀念过去。

争议焦点：
• 项目是否值得：部分用户认为复兴旧平台是怀旧且有趣的，但实用性不强；而另一部分用户则支持这些复兴项目，认为它们有技术和历史价值。
• 开源与闭源：部分用户对某些复兴项目未开源表示不满，认为这违背了互联网自由和开放的精神。

44590678.article_summary: 这篇文章宣布了一个项目，旨在重现昔日的即时通讯平台，如AOL Instant Messenger (AIM)、ICQ、Yahoo Messenger和经典AOL客户端。项目团队正在努力尽可能接近原版重建这些服务，并记录整个过程。目前，AIM和ICQ已可自由使用，其中ICQ仍在开发中；AOL 4.0和5.0的支持处于alpha阶段，仅对支持者开放；Yahoo Messenger已公开可用并与Escargot网络互通。文章还提到Q-Link（Commodore 64上的AOL前身）以及提供社交平台和社区支持，包括Discord、Reddit、论坛和Wiki。

不同观点：
• [怀旧与复兴支持者] lukaslalinsky怀念Jabber短暂兴盛的时代，认为那段时间的跨平台互通体验非常好，尽管很快结束。同时，bobsmith432提到现在有开发者在逆向工程Skype，并分享相关项目链接。
• [开源与闭源争议] fishgoesblub批评某些复兴项目未开源，并提到目前有开源的AIM服务器项目。marcodiego也质疑为何不贡献于现有的自由开源软件（FLOSS）实现，而是重新构建旧平台。
• [怀旧但怀疑实用性] iforgotpassword认为这些复兴项目虽然酷，但有点“毫无意义”，因为过去的体验无法完全重现，怀旧情绪更适合偶尔回忆。benguild同样认为，曾经的用户群体无法重现，体验无法回到过去。

data.title: The limits of our personal experience and the value of statistics
data.author: alphabetatango
data.article_summary: 文章指出，依赖个人经验了解世界是有限的，因为世界很大，而个人经验非常有限。即使我们每天与三个人交谈，一生也只能接触到0.001%的世界人口。因此，要全面了解世界，我们需要借助全球统计数据和其他媒体形式。个人互动虽然能拓展视野，但仍不足以覆盖广泛的世界。新闻媒体虽然帮助我们看到更远的地方，但其报道往往片面且偏向不寻常的事件，导致我们对世界的理解可能有偏差。文章强调，统计数据和多样化的媒体来源对于构建全面的世界观至关重要。

44591884.article_content:
It’s tempting to believe that we can simply rely on personal experience to develop our understanding of the world. But that’s a mistake. The world is large, and we can experience only very little of it personally. To see what the world is like, we need to rely on other means: carefully-collected global statistics.
Of course, our personal interactions are part of what informs our worldview. We piece together a picture of the lives of others around us from our interactions with them. Every time we meet people and hear about their lives, we add one more perspective to our worldview. This is a great way to see the world and expand our understanding, I don’t want to suggest otherwise. But I want to remind ourselves how little we can learn about our society through personal interactions alone, and how valuable statistics are in helping us build the rest of the picture.
The horizon of our personal experience
How many people do you know personally?
Let’s take a broad definition of what it means to know someone and say that we include everyone you know by name. A study in the US asked how many people Americans know by name and found that the average person knows 611.
1
Let’s assume you are more social than the average American, and you know 800 people. In a world of 8 billion, this means that you know 0.00001% of the population. A 100,000th of a percent.
2
It’s hard to visualize how small a fraction this is. If this illustration was drawn to scale, then the blue rectangle – which represents the world population – would be as large as a sheet of printer paper, while the yellow square – which represents the number that a person knows – would have the diameter of a human hair.
3
This is why I’m very skeptical when people say things about “the world these days” based on what they hear from people they know.
We cannot see much of the world through our direct experience. The horizon of our personal experience is very narrow. For every person you know, there are ten million people you do not know.
And chances are that the people you know are quite similar to you, far from representative of the world — or your country — as a whole.
Download image
How wide can the horizon of our personal experience be?
Perhaps you think restricting the people you learn from to the number of people you know by name is too narrow. After all, you also learn from strangers you meet, even if you don’t get to know their names.
Let’s assume you are exceptionally good at this, and you have a conversation with three new people every single day of your life.
If you can keep this up for 73 years, you will get to know 80,000 people.
4
That’s more than a hundred times the number of people you’d know by name.
This is still a tiny fraction of the world. After a lifetime of speaking with people, you will have spoken to 0.001% of the world’s population. For every person you’ve had a conversation with, there are still 100,000 people you’ve never spoken to.
Drawn to scale, the orange square, which represents the number of people you could ever speak to, would be less than a millimeter (0.8mm) wide.
5
I am focusing on personal interaction as the most direct and in-depth way to learn about others, but they are not our only experience by which we learn about others. We also learn by seeing other peoples’ clothes, by seeing their houses, or by hearing others talk about their personal experiences. But while these experiences also help, they still don’t get us very far. The world is large, and even if you are exceptionally attentive and exceptionally good at making connections and speaking to people, it is simply impossible to see much of the world directly.
Download image
The fragmented perspective of the news media: some spotlights on particular people, but much of the world is left in darkness
The limits of our personal experience don’t reach far beyond ourselves. How can we know about the world if we want to see beyond this tight horizon?
In one way or another, we have to rely on the media. Whether it is television or radio, the newspaper or photography, books, podcasts, documentaries, research papers, statistical tables, or social media.
This fact is so obvious that it is easy to miss how important it is: everything you hear about anyone who is more than a few dozen meters away, you know through some form of media.
That’s why the media we choose to rely on is
so
important for our understanding of the world.
The news is the media that shapes our picture of the world more than any other. Today, it’s often intertwined with social media. It is valuable as it lets us see beyond our own tight horizon, but the view the news offers is a spotted and fragmented one.
The news reports on the unusual things that happen on a
particular
day, but the things that happen
every
day never get mentioned. This gives us a biased and incomplete picture of the world; we are inundated with detailed news
on terrorism

data.title: Terence Tao: Game theory, politics and control of information
data.author: bertman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏理论及其在不同情境中的应用，包括冲突策略、游戏类型、信息操控以及身份认同对游戏的影响。

不同观点：
• [7402] 引用了Thomas Schelling的《冲突的战略》一书，指出信息劣势或决策自由的减少有时反而能增强一方的地位。他通过具体的讨论说明了这一反常现象，强调了信息不对称在博弈中的潜在优势。
• [andsoitis] 提出了两种游戏原型：有限游戏和无限游戏。有限游戏有明确的规则、开始和结束，而无限游戏的目的是延续游戏本身，规则可变且玩家可以随时加入或退出。这种分类扩展了对游戏本质理解的视野，尤其强调了规则和边界的流动性。
• [like_any_other] 批评了Tao对身份认同的忽视，指出玩家会形成团队，而如果能够通过瓦解对手的身份认同来使其单独行动，同时保持自己的团队认同，基本上就是赢得了游戏。此观点突出了身份认同在博弈中的战略重要性。
• [photonthug] 认为当前的博弈论概述过于高层次，缺乏对实际动态的系统研究。他强调了新兴的认知博弈论和社交媒体操控模型的重要性，并提出了对健康与不健康官僚机构的区分以及对AI系统中信念建模的关注。

补充讨论：
• 关于游戏理论的实际应用，[photonthug] 提到了TLA+风格的模型检查引擎MCMAS，并询问是否有类似的软件套件用于博弈理论分析和建模，特别是涉及信念和知识的复杂系统。
• 争议的焦点之一在于“理性行为者”假设的局限性，[photonthug] 指出该假设在解释现实世界动态时显得不足，尤其是在政治、误导信息以及高层次经济政策中的应用。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对管理科学的批评，认为其未能有效区分健康与不健康的官僚机构，以及对系统生命周期的研究不足。

以上观点展示了博弈论在不同领域的广泛应用及其在理解复杂社会动态中的潜在价值。

data.title: Numbers from my recent job hunt
data.author: Shane325
data.article_summary: 作者分享了他在2025年找工作的经历和相关数据。他从1月份开始全职找工作，6月份收到并签署了一份高级软件工程师的offer，整个过程大约6个月，但实际密集找工作的时间为3到4个月。他提交了73份申请，收到48个回复，进入10次面试，最终拿到1个offer。作者强调，内推是非常有效的方式，直接申请往往效果不佳。他建议不要广撒网式地申请大量职位，而是要善于利用内推资源，多次挖掘个人网络。即使感觉内推用尽，也可以反复寻找新的机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：求职过程中建立人脉和获取推荐的有效性

不同观点：
• willprice89 认为，在当前的就业市场中，"广撒网"的策略不起作用。他提出，如果在求职时没有稳固的人脉网络可以获取推荐，那么首要任务应该是参加社交活动来建立这样的人脉网络。

• bix6 的评论则反映了对于推荐作用的怀疑态度，可能基于个人经验或对数据有效性的关注，显示出对人脉推荐效果的不同看法。
• 争议的焦点在于推荐在求职过程中到底有多大的实际作用，以及是否应将建立人脉作为求职的首要任务。

44589704.article_content:
Numbers from my recent job hunt
17 Jul, 2025
I recently started a new job as a Senior Software Engineer at
Headway
. Now that I'm a few weeks into my new gig I thought it might be fun to share some numbers from my job hunt.
I started job hunting full time in January 2025 and signed an offer in June 2025. A bit less than 6 months from start to finish. Although, I wasn't actively applying for jobs during all of that time so it's probably closer to 3 or 4 months of intensive job search stuff.
Here's the numbers at a high level:
Total applications submitted: 73
Responses received: 48
Interviews (not counting recruiter screens): 10
Offer stage: 3
Offers: 1
And here's a nice funnel graphic:
The above graphic is broken down by application type. My number one take away from this job hunt was
referrals are very powerful
and by far the most effective way to get to the interview rounds. I did apply directly to some roles but I quickly realized that that method was a waste of time and stopped. I cringe when I see people post on LinkedIn that they've submitted 800 applications and not heard back. Please don't do that. Unfortunately, the spray and pray method will not work in this job market.
A number of times I thought that I had tapped out my potential referrals, but ended up combing back through my network a 2nd, 3rd, or 4th time. I always ended up finding new referrals.
Feel free to contact me with any questions and I'll be happy to expand on any of the above numbers and offer some (maybe) helpful advice.
7

Engineers have created a new type of
robot
that places living fungi behind the controls.
The
biohybrid robot
uses electrical signals from an edible type of mushroom called a king trumpet in order to move around and sense its environment.
Developed by an interdisciplinary team from Cornell University in the US and Florence University in Italy, the machine could herald a new era of living robotics.
“Living systems respond to touch, they respond to light, they respond to heat, they respond to even some unknowns, like signals,” said Anand Mishra, a research associate in the Organic Robotics Lab at Cornell.
“That’s why we think, OK, if you wanted to build future
robots
, how can they work in an unexpected environment? We can leverage these living systems, and any unknown input comes in, the robot will respond to that.”
Researchers from Cornell University in the US and the University of Florence in Italy placed a species of edible mushroom within a robot body
(
Robert Shepherd
)
Different inputs, such as ultraviolet light, resulted in different outcomes for the way the robot moved. A video of one of the mushroom-controlled robots shows it moving slowly across a surface by pumping its robotic legs. Another biohybrid robot uses a wheeled system in order to move around.
Combining this mobility with the fungi’s ability to sense chemical and biological signals could prove useful in a range of applications, according to the researchers.
“By growing mycelium into the electronics of a robot, we were able to allow the biohybrid machine to sense and respond to the environment,” said Rob Shepherd, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at Cornell.
“The potential for future robots could be to sense soil chemistry in row crops and decide when to add more fertiliser, for example, perhaps mitigating downstream effects of agriculture like harmful algal blooms.”
Details of the biohybrid robot were published in the journal
Science Robotics
, in
a study
titled ‘Sensorimotor control of robots mediated by electro-physiological measurements of fungal mycelia’.
It is not the first time a living organism has been placed inside a robot body, though the use of mushrooms could offer a major breakthrough in the field of biohybrid robotics due to their ability to grow and survive in harsh conditions.
Previous experiments have included
an artificial worm brain placed inside a Lego robot
, which was able to recreate the creature’s movements and intentions.
Earlier this year, researchers from Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) created a machine that was integrated with living muscle tissue in order to sense and adapt to its environment.

data.title: LLM Daydreaming
data.author: nanfinitum
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLM）在创新和发现能力上的缺失，特别是缺乏人类思维中的“默认模式网络”和持续学习能力。作者提出了一种“白日梦循环”（Day-Dreaming Loop, DDL）机制，通过后台进程不断从记忆中抽取概念对，并通过生成模型和批评模型探索和筛选有价值的联系，形成反馈循环，以产生新颖的想法。尽管这种过程成本高昂，但可能是创新的必要代价。文章还指出，LLM由于“冻结”状态而无法从经验中学习，并且缺乏持续思考的能力，这限制了它们产生重大突破的能力。最终，作者建议构建能够进行“浪费性”后台搜索的AI系统，以生成专有训练数据，从而绕过数据壁垒。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）是否带来了突破性进展，及其在创造力和新颖性方面的能力。

不同观点：
• 一些用户认为LLMs已经带来了实际的突破，但这些突破可能未被充分认可。例如，ashdksnndck指出，人们在使用LLMs得到好的结果时，往往不会特别注明这些想法来自模型，因为模型被视为一种工具，就像其他任何技术一样。
• HarHarVeryFunny和throwaway328则持相反观点，认为LLMs本质上是预测下一个词的语言模型，缺乏创造性和真正的突破能力。他们强调，LLMs的设计初衷是 recall（回忆）而非创造，因此期待其产生真正的创新是不现实的。
• zhangjunphy和OtherShrezzing指出，利用LLMs作为批评模型或进行创新研究的尝试往往不成功，因为这些模型在满足批评标准时表现不佳，且大规模应用也仅带来边际改进。

补充讨论：
• 关于如何评估LLMs的输出和新颖性，jumploops和A_D_E_P_T提到，识别独特见解需要高水平的专业知识和适当的提示。此外，LLMs在跨学科和新颖概念组合方面的能力有限，这也是其难以产生突破的原因之一。
• pilooch和sartak则探讨了结合不同算法和LLMs的可能性，认为通过搜索空间和进化算法等方法，可能在某些领域取得进展。
• 对于LLMs的批评和期望，velcrovan推荐阅读David Gelernter的著作，认为其探讨了创造性计算的可能性，而blueflow和cranium则对LLMs在数据评估和项目改进方面的表现提出质疑。

争议焦点：
• LLMs是否具备真正的创造力和产生突破性进展的潜力。
• 如何有效评估和利用LLMs的输出，以及在什么情况下LLMs能发挥最大作用。

整体来看，讨论围绕LLMs的能力和局限性展开，反映了对其潜力和现实应用的不同期望和看法。

Proposal & discussion of how default mode networks for LLMs are an example of missing capabilities for search and novelty in contemporary AI systems.
2025-07-12–2025-07-14
